107|## The checklist
108|
109|Fill it in for each piece of code you inspect, so that no piece is judged without its neighbours:
110|
111|- **Callers:** who calls it, and with what shapes at 1, 8 and 32 rows.
112|- **Callees:** what it calls, down to the Metal kernel it launches.
113|- **Data:** each input and output with shape, dtype and layout. Where it is produced, and where it is consumed next.
114|- **Neighbours:** what runs just before and after it in the decode step, and what a replacement must keep identical.
115|- **Cost:** the kernels it launches, the bytes it reads and writes (weight bytes counted per read), and its measured time with the table the time comes from.
116|- **Invariants:** what correctness depends on: the G2 tolerances, the tie rule for the 4th and 5th expert, the bfloat16 rounding points.

132|2. Then change direction when:

134|   - **its premise fell:** the claim your work rests on was refuted;
135|   - **something pays more:** an open item in your territory or task predicts a larger saving than what you're on, and nobody owns it.

143|- **Only the lead commits.** Helpers never run `git add` or `git commit`.

146|- **Credentials stay unread:** `.env` files, `~/.config/muse/` and any key store.

1|# Hypothesis 2: fused routing kernel
2|
3|- **Owner:** lead
4|- **Status:** building

9|## Inefficiency
10|
11|Slot `routing`. One entry:
12|
13|- `ineff-runs-2` (rank 2, mean 11.0% of step): routing costs 1.02 ms at 1 row and 1.68 ms at 32 rows while reading ~4 MB — 12 tiny kernels/layer of pure overhead (argpartition runs a full 60-element sort per row; the weights-norm sum runs on 1 thread at 1 row). Fusion to ~1 kernel/layer saves 0.9 / 1.2 / 1.4 ms at 1/8/32 rows.
14|
15|Design: one Metal kernel per layer that computes router scores (matmul + sigmoid + bias), selects the top-4 experts, and normalizes/scales the weights, with the 4 experts in any order per row. G2 gives freedom only on within-1e-6 tie rows and 1e-4 relative weights by expert.
16|
17|## Boundary
18|
19|*written by boundary-2, 2026-11-03T21:45Z*
20|
21|### Inputs and outputs
22|
23|Source: the brief's routing table (`claude/muse-agent-brief.md:28-36`) and `bench/grader/slots.py:19-48`. All arrays row-contiguous (brief:24).
24|
25|| | Name | Shape at 1 / 8 / 32 rows | Dtype | Layout |
26||---|---|---|---|---|
27|| input | `x` | [1,768] / [8,768] / [32,768] | bfloat16 | flat rows of the MoE input, row-contiguous |
28|| input | `w_router` | [60,768] at all row counts | float32 | router weight, used transposed (`x @ w_router.T`) |
29|| input | `bias` | [60] at all row counts | float32 (the model's bfloat16 `expert_bias`, converted exactly) | one value per expert |
30|| output | `inds` | [1,4] / [8,4] / [32,4] | uint32 | 4 expert indices per row, each < 60 |
31|| output | `weights` | [1,4] / [8,4] / [32,4] | float32 | `weights[r,j]` belongs to `inds[r,j]` |
32|
33|### Before and after in `MoE.__call__`
34|
35|Source: `third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/mobilemoe.py:217-232` and the split harness `bench/grader/slots.py:105-119`.
36|
37|- **Before:** the slot input `x` is the MoE block's input, i.e. `post_attention_layernorm(h)` reshaped to flat `[rows,768]` (`mobilemoe.py:258-260`, `slots.py:106-107`). `w_router` (`self.router.weight`) and `bias` (`self.expert_bias.astype(float32)`, `slots.py:108`) are parameters. The producer expects nothing back; the slot must read `x` as bfloat16 — the reference casts to float32 itself (`mobilemoe.py:219`).
38|- **After (1), the experts call:** `SwitchGLU(x, inds)` gathers expert weights per (row, j) by index (`switch_layers.py:176-199`). From `inds.size >= 64` (rows ≥ 16) it sorts pairs by expert internally and unscatters the result back, so its output `y[..., j, :]` always corresponds to `inds[..., j]` whatever per-row order the slot emits (brief:53: `y` is "in `inds` order"). It expects 4 valid indices per row, each < 60; order is free.
39|- **After (2), combine:** `(y * weights[..., None]).sum(axis=-2).astype(bfloat16) + shared` (`mobilemoe.py:231`, `slots.py:51-52`). It expects `weights[r,j]` to be the normalized weight of `inds[r,j]` (brief:47). The shared expert runs independently of the slot.
40|
41|Checklist (per `tracking.md`) for each neighbour:
42|
43|- **Producer (layernorm output / MoE entry).** Callers: `DecoderLayer.__call__` (`mobilemoe.py:258-260`). Callees: none into the slot — it only supplies `x`. Data: `x` [rows,768] bf16. Neighbours: attention block before (untouched). Cost: outside the slot. Invariants: `x` values are whatever the model produces; no assumption about their range beyond bf16.
44|- **Consumer `SwitchGLU(x, inds)`.** Callers: `MoE.__call__` (`mobilemoe.py:230`). Callees: `gather_qmm` per product, with internal sort/unsort from rows ≥ 16 (`switch_layers.py:176-199`). Data: `inds` [rows,4] uint32. Neighbours: combine after it. Cost: the experts slot (hyp-1), untouched by this hypothesis. Invariants: one output row per (row, j) pair, in `inds` order; any per-row permutation of `inds` is safe as long as `weights` permutes with it.
45|- **Consumer combine.** Callers: `MoE.__call__` (`mobilemoe.py:231`). Callees: none (reference arithmetic). Data: `weights` [rows,4] f32, `y` [rows,4,768] bf16, `shared` [rows,768] bf16. Neighbours: residual add `h + ...` in `DecoderLayer` after. Cost: 5 kernels/layer, untouched. Invariants: the bf16 cast happens here, outside the slot — the slot outputs pure float32.
46|
47|### What must stay identical
48|
49|- **Rounding points:** everything inside the slot is float32 — `x` cast bf16→f32 (exact), matmul + sigmoid in f32, gather of the *unbiased* scores, f32 sum/divide (epsilon 1e-20) and × 2.5 (`slots.py:44-48`, `mobilemoe.py:219-228`). There is no bf16 rounding inside the slot; the only cast is combine's `.astype(bfloat16)`, outside the slot. So reduced precision anywhere in the fused kernel is allowed only if weights still land within 1e-4 relative per expert; a different summation order is fine within that tolerance.
50|- **The bias rule:** the bias changes *which* experts are selected, not their weights (`mobilemoe.py:221-225`): selection uses `scores + bias`, weights use the unbiased `scores` gathered at the selected indices.
51|- **Tie rule:** each row must select the same 4-expert *set* as the reference top-4 of biased scores, except rows where the reference's 4th and 5th biased scores are within 1e-6 of each other (brief:183, `check_candidate.py:67-80`). The 4 indices per row must be distinct and < 60 (`check_candidate.py:65`).
52|- **Allowed reorderings:** any permutation of the 4 (row, j) pairs within a row; the `inds[r,j]` ↔ `weights[r,j]` pairing must be preserved (brief:47). Nothing else may move: the slot may not change shapes, dtypes, the epsilon, the 2.5 scale, or the unbiased-score rule.
53|
54|### What the grader checks, and what it can't see
55|
56|- **G1** compiles the Metal and runs it on the captured inputs at 1, 8 and 32 rows (brief:181, `check_candidate.py:206`).
57|- **G2 routing** checks exact shapes/dtypes, `inds < 60`, expert-set equality per row (near-tie rows counted and skipping the weight check), and weights by expert within 1e-4 relative (`check_candidate.py:50-94,133-138`). Inputs are captured from all 20 layers of one real decode step per row count (`slots.py:137-171`, brief:182). Piece timing (median of 30 × all-20-layers eval ÷ 20) must beat `mx.compile(ref_routing)` at all three row counts to stop the slot (brief:195, `check_candidate.py:209-226`).
58|- **What it can't see:** row counts other than 1, 8 and 32 — a decode step can have any row count from 1 to 32 (brief:24); inputs other than the captured ones (other prompts, later decode steps, other layers' drift); threadgroup-memory use near the 32 KB limit (`slots.build` enforces only the 1024-thread cap, `slots.py:275`); results that depend on thread timing; the end-to-end greedy-token check (24 tokens, plain MLX and vLLM) and G3 full-step timing, which the team runs after merging (brief:185-186,195). Boundary checks will probe exactly these.
59|
60|### The GPU limits
61|
62|At most 1,024 threads per threadgroup and 32 KB of threadgroup memory (brief:98); `grid` counts threads, not threadgroups (brief:175). Hardware: Apple M1 Pro, 16 cores, SIMD width 32, `bfloat` available in Metal (brief:99).

1|"""The parts of MobileMoE-S's MoE block that a Muse Spark kernel may replace.
2|
3|Each slot has a reference (the port's own code, split as in breakdown.py),
4|named inputs and outputs (claude/muse-agent-brief.md), and a way to install
5|an implementation into MoE.__call__ for every layer. build() turns a launch
6|spec (data, never code) into mx.fast.metal_kernel calls.
7|
8|Record the grader's inputs from a real decode step (plain MLX, no API):
9|
10|  .venv/bin/python bench/grader/slots.py capture
11|"""
12|
13|import re
14|from pathlib import Path
15|
16|import mlx.core as mx
17|import numpy as np
18|
19|D, E, K, H = 768, 60, 4, 384
20|SCALE = 2.5  # routed_scaling_factor; norm_topk_prob is true
21|NAMES = {"D": D, "E": E, "K": K, "H": H}
22|DTYPES = {
23|    "float32": mx.float32,
24|    "bfloat16": mx.bfloat16,
25|    "float16": mx.float16,
26|    "uint32": mx.uint32,
27|    "int32": mx.int32,
28|}
29|SLOTS = {
30|    "routing": (["x", "w_router", "bias"], ["inds", "weights"]),
31|    "combine": (["y", "weights", "shared"], ["out"]),
32|}
33|EXPERT_WEIGHTS = [
34|    f"{p}_{t}" for p in ("gate", "up", "down") for t in ("w", "scales", "biases")
35|]
36|SLOTS["experts"] = (["x", "inds"] + EXPERT_WEIGHTS, ["y"])
37|SLOTS["routing+combine"] = (
38|    SLOTS["routing"][0] + ["y", "shared"],
39|    ["inds", "weights", "out"],
40|)
41|INPUTS = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "models" / "muse-inputs"

44|def ref_routing(x, w_router, bias):
45|    scores = mx.sigmoid(x.astype(mx.float32) @ w_router.T)
46|    inds = mx.argpartition(-(scores + bias), kth=K - 1, axis=-1)[:, :K]
47|    w = mx.take_along_axis(scores, inds, axis=-1)
48|    return inds, w / (w.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True) + 1e-20) * SCALE
49|
50|
51|def ref_combine(y, weights, shared):
52|    return (y * weights[..., None]).sum(axis=-2).astype(mx.bfloat16) + shared
53|
54|
55|def ref_experts(x, inds, *weights):
56|    """The port's SwitchGLU on flat rows: [rows, D] and [rows, K] -> [rows, K, D]."""
57|    from mlx_lm.models.activations import swiglu
58|    from mlx_lm.models.switch_layers import _gather_sort, _scatter_unsort
59|
60|    gate, up, down = weights[0:3], weights[3:6], weights[6:9]
61|    xx = mx.expand_dims(x, (-2, -3))
62|    do_sort = inds.size >= 64
63|    idx, inv = inds, None
64|    if do_sort:
65|        xx, idx, inv = _gather_sort(xx, inds)
66|
67|    def qmm(a, w):
68|        return mx.gather_qmm(
69|            a,
70|            *w,
71|            rhs_indices=idx,
72|            transpose=False,
73|            group_size=32,
74|            bits=4,
75|            mode="affine",
76|            sorted_indices=do_sort,
77|        )
78|
79|    y = qmm(swiglu(qmm(xx, gate), qmm(xx, up)), down)
80|    if do_sort:
81|        y = _scatter_unsort(y, inv, inds.shape)
82|    return y.squeeze(-2)
83|
84|
85|REFERENCE = {"routing": ref_routing, "combine": ref_combine, "experts": ref_experts}

88|def expert_weights(experts):
89|    """A layer's SwitchGLU weights, named as in the experts slot."""
90|    return {
91|        f"{p}_{t}": getattr(experts, f"{p}_proj")[k]
92|        for p in ("gate", "up", "down")
93|        for t, k in (("w", "weight"), ("scales", "scales"), ("biases", "biases"))
94|    }

97|def make_moe_call(routing=ref_routing, combine=ref_combine, experts=None):
98|    """MoE.__call__ with its slots swapped for *routing*, *combine*, *experts*.
99|
100|    With the references it gives the port's outputs bit for bit (checked by
101|    check_identity), so any difference comes from the swapped slot. With
102|    experts=None the port's own SwitchGLU runs.
103|    """
104|
105|    def moe_call(self, x):
106|        lead = x.shape[:-1]
107|        flat = x.reshape(-1, D)
108|        bias = self.expert_bias.astype(mx.float32)
109|        inds, weights = routing(flat, self.router.weight, bias)
110|        if experts is None:
111|            y = self.experts(x, inds.reshape(*lead, K))
112|        else:
113|            w = expert_weights(self.experts)
114|            y = experts(flat, inds, *[w[n] for n in EXPERT_WEIGHTS])
115|        shared = self.shared_expert(x)
116|        out = combine(y.reshape(-1, K, D), weights, shared.reshape(-1, D))
117|        return out.reshape(*lead, D)
118|
119|    return moe_call

122|def check_identity(model):
123|    """The split MoE with reference slots equals the port's, at 1, 8, 32 rows."""
124|    from mlx_lm.models import mobilemoe
125|
126|    original = mobilemoe.MoE.__call__
127|    for split in (make_moe_call(), make_moe_call(experts=ref_experts)):
128|        for rows in (1, 8, 32):
129|            moe = model.model.layers[3].feed_forward
130|            x = mx.random.normal((1, rows, D)).astype(mx.bfloat16)
131|            if not mx.array_equal(original(moe, x), split(moe, x)).item():
132|                raise AssertionError(
133|                    f"split MoE differs from the port's at {rows} rows"
134|                )

137|def capture(model, rows, step=8, seed=None):
138|    """Every layer's slot inputs and reference outputs in one real decode step."""
139|    import sys
140|
141|    sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "micro"))
142|    import breakdown as bd
143|    from mlx_lm.models import mobilemoe
144|    from mlx_lm.models.cache import make_prompt_cache
145|
146|    original = mobilemoe.MoE.__call__
147|    seen = []
148|
149|    def recording_routing(x, w_router, bias):
150|        inds, weights = ref_routing(x, w_router, bias)
151|        seen.append({"x": x, "w_router": w_router, "bias": bias, "inds": inds})
152|        return inds, weights
153|
154|    def recording_combine(y, weights, shared):
155|        seen[-1].update(y=y, weights_in=weights, shared=shared)
156|        return ref_combine(y, weights, shared)
157|
158|    mx.random.seed(rows if seed is None else seed)
159|    ids = mx.random.randint(0, 100000, (rows, 128))
160|    cache = make_prompt_cache(model)
161|    y = bd.prefill(model, ids, cache)
162|    for _ in range(step - 1):
163|        y = bd.greedy(model(y, cache=cache))
164|        mx.eval(y)
165|    mobilemoe.MoE.__call__ = make_moe_call(recording_routing, recording_combine)
166|    try:
167|        logits = model(y, cache=cache)
168|        mx.eval(logits, [list(s.values()) for s in seen])
169|    finally:
170|        mobilemoe.MoE.__call__ = original
171|    return seen

174|def save_inputs(model):
175|    INPUTS.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
176|    for rows in (1, 8, 32):
177|        layers = capture(model, rows)

179|            f"L{i:02d}_{k}": np.array(

181|            )
182|            for i, layer in enumerate(layers)
183|            for k, v in layer.items()
184|        }
185|        np.savez(INPUTS / f"rows{rows}.npz", **arrays)

205|def load_inputs(rows, with_weights=None):
206|    """[{name: mx.array}] per layer, with bfloat16 restored where the model had it.
207|
208|    *with_weights*, from load_expert_weights, adds each layer's expert weights.
209|    """
210|    data = np.load(INPUTS / f"rows{rows}.npz")
211|    bf16 = {"x", "y", "shared"}
212|    layers = {}
213|    for key in data.files:
214|        i, name = int(key[1:3]), key[4:]
215|        a = mx.array(data[key])
216|        layers.setdefault(i, {})[name] = a.astype(mx.bfloat16) if name in bf16 else a
217|    for i, layer in layers.items():
218|        layer["weights"] = layer.pop("weights_in")
219|        if "inds" in layer:
220|            layer["inds"] = layer["inds"].astype(mx.uint32)
221|        if with_weights is not None:
222|            layer.update(with_weights[i])
223|    return [layers[i] for i in sorted(layers)]

226|# Muse Spark's launch spec: integers, or products of integers and NAMES/rows.
227|TERM = re.compile(r"^(\d+|rows|D|E|K|H)$")
228|
229|
230|def dim(expr, rows):
231|    if isinstance(expr, bool) or not isinstance(expr, (int, str)):
232|        raise ValueError(f"bad size {expr!r}")
233|    if isinstance(expr, int):
234|        return expr
235|    value = 1
236|    for term in expr.replace(" ", "").split("*"):
237|        if not TERM.match(term):
238|            raise ValueError(f"bad size term {term!r} in {expr!r}")
239|        value *= rows if term == "rows" else NAMES.get(term) or int(term)
240|    return value
241|
242|
243|def template_value(v):
244|    if isinstance(v, bool) or isinstance(v, int):
245|        return v
246|    if isinstance(v, str) and v in DTYPES:
247|        return DTYPES[v]
248|    raise ValueError(f"bad template value {v!r}")
249|
250|
251|def build(spec, sources, slot):
252|    """A function slot_inputs -> slot_outputs from Muse Spark's spec and Metal blocks."""
253|    slot_in, slot_out = SLOTS[slot]
254|    kernels = []
255|    for k in spec["kernels"]:
256|        header = "" if k.get("header_block") is None else sources[k["header_block"]]
257|        fn = mx.fast.metal_kernel(
258|            name=re.sub(r"\W", "_", str(k["name"])),
259|            input_names=list(k["inputs"]),
260|            output_names=[o["name"] for o in k["outputs"]],
261|            source=sources[k["source_block"]],
262|            header=header,
263|            atomic_outputs=bool(k.get("atomic_outputs", False)),
264|        )
265|        kernels.append((k, fn))
266|    missing = set(slot_out) - set(spec["slot_outputs"])
267|    if missing:
268|        raise ValueError(f"slot_outputs is missing {sorted(missing)}")
269|
270|    def run(**inputs):
271|        rows = inputs[slot_in[0]].shape[0]
272|        env = dict(inputs)
273|        for k, fn in kernels:
274|            tg = [int(t) for t in k["threadgroup"]]
275|            if any(t < 1 for t in tg) or tg[0] * tg[1] * tg[2] > 1024:
276|                raise ValueError(f"bad threadgroup {tg}")
277|            outs = fn(
278|                inputs=[env[n] for n in k["inputs"]],
279|                template=[
280|                    (n, template_value(v)) for n, v in (k.get("template") or {}).items()
281|                ],
282|                grid=tuple(dim(g, rows) for g in k["grid"]),
283|                threadgroup=tuple(tg),
284|                output_shapes=[
285|                    tuple(dim(s, rows) for s in o["shape"]) for o in k["outputs"]
286|                ],
287|                output_dtypes=[DTYPES[o["dtype"]] for o in k["outputs"]],
288|                init_value=k.get("init_value"),
289|            )
290|            env.update(zip([o["name"] for o in k["outputs"]], outs))
291|        return {name: env[src] for name, src in spec["slot_outputs"].items()}
292|
293|    return run
294|

45|- **Consumer combine.** Callers: `MoE.__call__` (`mobilemoe.py:231`). Callees: none (reference arithmetic). Data: `weights` [rows,4] f32, `y` [rows,4,768] bf16, `shared` [rows,768] bf16. Neighbours: residual add `h + ...` in `DecoderLayer` after. Cost: 5 kernels/layer, untouched. Invariants: the bf16 cast happens here, outside the slot — the slot outputs pure float32.

47|### What must stay identical
48|
49|- **Rounding points:** everything inside the slot is float32 — `x` cast bf16→f32 (exact), matmul + sigmoid in f32, gather of the *unbiased* scores, f32 sum/divide (epsilon 1e-20) and × 2.5 (`slots.py:44-48`, `mobilemoe.py:219-228`). There is no bf16 rounding inside the slot; the only cast is combine's `.astype(bfloat16)`, outside the slot. So reduced precision anywhere in the fused kernel is allowed only if weights still land within 1e-4 relative per expert; a different summation order is fine within that tolerance.
50|- **The bias rule:** the bias changes *which* experts are selected, not their weights (`mobilemoe.py:221-225`): selection uses `scores + bias`, weights use the unbiased `scores` gathered at the selected indices.
51|- **Tie rule:** each row must select the same 4-expert *set* as the reference top-4 of biased scores, except rows where the reference's 4th and 5th biased scores are within 1e-6 of each other (brief:183, `check_candidate.py:67-80`). The 4 indices per row must be distinct and < 60 (`check_candidate.py:65`).
52|- **Allowed reorderings:** any permutation of the 4 (row, j) pairs within a row; the `inds[r,j]` ↔ `weights[r,j]` pairing must be preserved (brief:47). Nothing else may move: the slot may not change shapes, dtypes, the epsilon, the 2.5 scale, or the unbiased-score rule.
53|
54|### What the grader checks, and what it can't see
55|
56|- **G1** compiles the Metal and runs it on the captured inputs at 1, 8 and 32 rows (brief:181, `check_candidate.py:206`).
57|- **G2 routing** checks exact shapes/dtypes, `inds < 60`, expert-set equality per row (near-tie rows counted and skipping the weight check), and weights by expert within 1e-4 relative (`check_candidate.py:50-94,133-138`). Inputs are captured from all 20 layers of one real decode step per row count (`slots.py:137-171`, brief:182). Piece timing (median of 30 × all-20-layers eval ÷ 20) must beat `mx.compile(ref_routing)` at all three row counts to stop the slot (brief:195, `check_candidate.py:209-226`).
58|- **What it can't see:** row counts other than 1, 8 and 32 — a decode step can have any row count from 1 to 32 (brief:24); inputs other than the captured ones (other prompts, later decode steps, other layers' drift); threadgroup-memory use near the 32 KB limit (`slots.build` enforces only the 1024-thread cap, `slots.py:275`); results that depend on thread timing; the end-to-end greedy-token check (24 tokens, plain MLX and vLLM) and G3 full-step timing, which the team runs after merging (brief:185-186,195). Boundary checks will probe exactly these.

60|### The GPU limits
61|
62|At most 1,024 threads per threadgroup and 32 KB of threadgroup memory (brief:98); `grid` counts threads, not threadgroups (brief:175). Hardware: Apple M1 Pro, 16 cores, SIMD width 32, `bfloat` available in Metal (brief:99).

1|"""Grade one kernel attempt: compile it, test it on captured inputs, time it.
2|
3|The independent grader for Muse Spark's kernels (claude/muse-agent-brief.md).
4|It runs on the inputs `slots.py capture` recorded from a real decode step,
5|prints its verdict as JSON, and writes it to --out when given. It never
6|writes into the attempt folder, which holds only Muse Spark's files.
7|
8|  .venv/bin/python bench/grader/check_candidate.py muse-spark/kernels/<slot>/attempt-N <slot> [--out FILE]
9|"""
10|
11|import argparse
12|import json
13|import statistics
14|import sys
15|import time
16|import traceback
17|from pathlib import Path
18|
19|import mlx.core as mx
20|import numpy as np
21|
22|sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
23|import gpu_lock  # noqa: E402
24|import slots  # noqa: E402
25|
26|ROWS = (1, 8, 32)
27|REPEATS = 30
28|
29|
30|def parts(slot):
31|    return ["routing", "combine"] if slot == "routing+combine" else [slot]
32|
33|
34|def load(attempt, slot):
35|    spec = json.loads((attempt / "spec.json").read_text())
36|    sources = [
37|        p.read_text()
38|        for p in sorted(attempt.glob("block-*.metal"), key=lambda p: int(p.stem[6:]))
39|    ]
40|    specs = spec if slot == "routing+combine" else {slot: spec}
41|    return {p: slots.build(specs[p], sources, p) for p in parts(slot)}
42|
43|
44|def ulp_bf16(r):
45|    """bfloat16's unit in the last place at |r|, floored at |r| = 0.001 (brief, G2)."""
46|    exp = np.floor(np.log2(np.maximum(np.abs(r), 1e-3)))
47|    return 2.0 ** (exp - 7)
48|
49|
50|def check_routing(fn, layer):
51|    ref_inds, ref_w = slots.ref_routing(layer["x"], layer["w_router"], layer["bias"])
52|    got = fn(x=layer["x"], w_router=layer["w_router"], bias=layer["bias"])
53|    inds, w = got["inds"], got["weights"]
54|    rows = layer["x"].shape[0]
55|    if inds.shape != (rows, slots.K) or w.shape != (rows, slots.K):
56|        return {
57|            "error": f"shapes inds {inds.shape}, weights {w.shape}; want ({rows}, 4)"
58|        }
59|    if inds.dtype != mx.uint32 or w.dtype != mx.float32:
60|        return {
61|            "error": f"dtypes inds {inds.dtype}, weights {w.dtype}; want uint32, float32"
62|        }
63|    inds, w = np.array(inds), np.array(w)
64|    ref_inds, ref_w = np.array(ref_inds), np.array(ref_w)
65|    if inds.max() >= slots.E:
66|        return {"error": f"expert index {int(inds.max())} out of range (60 experts)"}
67|    scores = np.array(mx.sigmoid(layer["x"].astype(mx.float32) @ layer["w_router"].T))
68|    biased = np.sort(scores + np.array(layer["bias"]), axis=-1)[:, ::-1]
69|    wrong, ties, worst, example = 0, 0, 0.0, None
70|    for r in range(rows):
71|        if set(inds[r]) != set(ref_inds[r]):
72|            if biased[r, 3] - biased[r, 4] < 1e-6:
73|                ties += 1
74|            else:
75|                wrong += 1
76|                example = example or (
77|                    f"row {r}: experts {sorted(inds[r].tolist())}, "
78|                    f"want {sorted(ref_inds[r].tolist())}"
79|                )
80|            continue
81|        ref = dict(zip(ref_inds[r], ref_w[r]))
82|        for e, v in zip(inds[r], w[r]):
83|            err = abs(v - ref[e]) / max(abs(ref[e]), 1e-12)
84|            if err > worst:
85|                worst = err
86|                if err > 1e-4:
87|                    example = f"row {r} expert {e}: weight {v:.7g}, want {ref[e]:.7g}"
88|    out = {
89|        "rows_wrong_experts": wrong,
90|        "near_tie_rows": ties,
91|        "max_rel_err": float(worst),
92|    }
93|    return out | ({"example": example} if example else {})
94|
95|
96|def check_combine(fn, layer):
97|    ref = slots.ref_combine(layer["y"], layer["weights"], layer["shared"])
98|    got = fn(y=layer["y"], weights=layer["weights"], shared=layer["shared"])["out"]
99|    if got.shape != ref.shape or got.dtype != mx.bfloat16:
100|        return {"error": f"out {got.shape} {got.dtype}; want {ref.shape} bfloat16"}
101|    r = np.array(ref.astype(mx.float32))
102|    g = np.array(got.astype(mx.float32))
103|    with np.errstate(over="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
104|        over = np.nan_to_num(np.abs(g - r) / ulp_bf16(r), nan=1e9, posinf=1e9)
105|    out = {"max_ulp": float(min(over.max(), 1e9)), "bad": int((over > 2).sum())}
106|    if out["bad"]:
107|        i, j = np.unravel_index(over.argmax(), over.shape)
108|        out["example"] = f"row {i} column {j}: {g[i, j]:.6g}, want {r[i, j]:.6g}"
109|    return out
110|
111|
112|def check_experts(fn, layer):
113|    names = slots.SLOTS["experts"][0]
114|    args = [layer[n] for n in names]
115|    ref = slots.ref_experts(*args)
116|    got = fn(**{n: layer[n] for n in names})["y"]
117|    if got.shape != ref.shape or got.dtype != mx.bfloat16:
118|        return {"error": f"y {got.shape} {got.dtype}; want {ref.shape} bfloat16"}
119|    r = np.array(ref.astype(mx.float32)).reshape(ref.shape[0], -1)
120|    g = np.array(got.astype(mx.float32)).reshape(ref.shape[0], -1)
121|    with np.errstate(over="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
122|        over = np.nan_to_num(np.abs(g - r) / ulp_bf16(r), nan=1e9, posinf=1e9)
123|    out = {"max_ulp": float(min(over.max(), 1e9)), "bad": int((over > 2).sum())}
124|    if out["bad"]:
125|        i, j = np.unravel_index(over.argmax(), over.shape)
126|        k, d = divmod(j, slots.D)
127|        out["example"] = (
128|            f"row {i} expert slot {k} column {d}: {g[i, j]:.6g}, want {r[i, j]:.6g}"
129|        )
130|    return out
131|
132|
133|def passes(part, s):
134|    if "error" in s:
135|        return False
136|    if part == "routing":
137|        return s["rows_wrong_experts"] == 0 and s["max_rel_err"] <= 1e-4
138|    return s["bad"] == 0
139|
140|
141|def timed(fn, layers, names):
142|    """Median µs per layer: all 20 layers' calls, then one wait for the GPU."""
143|    for _ in range(3):
144|        mx.eval([fn(**{n: layer[n] for n in names}) for layer in layers])
145|    times = []
146|    for _ in range(REPEATS):
147|        t0 = time.perf_counter()
148|        mx.eval([fn(**{n: layer[n] for n in names}) for layer in layers])
149|        times.append((time.perf_counter() - t0) / len(layers))
150|    return round(statistics.median(times) * 1e6, 1)
151|
152|
153|def short_error(e):
154|    """The exception, keeping only the compiler's error lines from Metal builds."""
155|    text = "".join(traceback.format_exception_only(type(e), e)).strip()
156|    lines = text.splitlines()
157|    if len(lines) > 1 and "Unable to build metal library" in lines[0]:
158|        keep = [lines[0]]
159|        for i, line in enumerate(lines):
160|            if "error:" in line:
161|                keep += lines[i : i + 3]
162|        text = "\n".join(keep)
163|    return text[:4000]
164|
165|
166|def main():
167|    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
168|    ap.add_argument("attempt", type=Path)
169|    ap.add_argument("slot", choices=tuple(slots.SLOTS))
170|    ap.add_argument("--out", type=Path, help="also write the verdict here")
171|    args = ap.parse_args()
172|    attempt, slot = args.attempt, args.slot
173|    gpu_lock.hold(f"check_candidate.py {attempt} {slot}")
174|    result = {"slot": slot, "g1": False, "g2": False, "beats_compiled": False}
175|    try:
176|        fns = load(attempt, slot)
177|        weights = slots.load_expert_weights() if slot == "experts" else None
178|        stats = {}
179|        for rows in ROWS:
180|            layers = slots.load_inputs(rows, weights)
181|            for part, fn in fns.items():
182|                check = {
183|                    "routing": check_routing,
184|                    "combine": check_combine,
185|                    "experts": check_experts,
186|                }[part]
187|                per_layer = [check(fn, layer) for layer in layers]
188|                errors = [s["error"] for s in per_layer if "error" in s]
189|                if errors:
190|                    stats[f"{part} rows {rows}"] = {"error": errors[0]}
191|                    continue
192|                agg = {
193|                    k: (max if k.startswith("max") else sum)(s[k] for s in per_layer)
194|                    for k in per_layer[0]
195|                    if k != "example"
196|                }
197|                agg["pass"] = all(passes(part, s) for s in per_layer)
198|                examples = [
199|                    f"layer {i}, {s['example']}"
200|                    for i, s in enumerate(per_layer)
201|                    if "example" in s
202|                ]
203|                if examples:
204|                    agg["worst_example"] = examples[0]
205|                stats[f"{part} rows {rows}"] = agg
206|        result["g1"] = True
207|        result["correctness"] = stats
208|        result["g2"] = all(s.get("pass") for s in stats.values())
209|        if result["g2"]:
210|            timing, beats = {}, True
211|            for rows in ROWS:
212|                layers = slots.load_inputs(rows, weights)
213|                row = {"reference": 0.0, "compiled": 0.0, "candidate": 0.0}
214|                for part, fn in fns.items():
215|                    names = slots.SLOTS[part][0]
216|                    ref = slots.REFERENCE[part]
217|                    wrap = lambda f: lambda **kw: f(
218|                        *[kw[n] for n in names]
219|                    )  # noqa: E731
220|                    row["reference"] += timed(wrap(ref), layers, names)
221|                    row["compiled"] += timed(wrap(mx.compile(ref)), layers, names)
222|                    row["candidate"] += timed(fn, layers, names)
223|                timing[f"rows {rows}"] = {k: round(v, 1) for k, v in row.items()}
224|                beats &= row["candidate"] < row["compiled"]
225|            result["timing_us_per_layer"] = timing
226|            result["beats_compiled"] = beats
227|    except Exception as e:  # report the failure to Muse Spark as G1
228|        result["error"] = short_error(e)
229|    if args.out:
230|        args.out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
231|        args.out.write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=1) + "\n")
232|    print(json.dumps(result))
233|

235|if __name__ == "__main__":
236|    main()

17|- `results/runs/2026-11-01-breakdown/tables.md` and `results/runs/2026-11-02-gpu-counters/tables.md`: the raw tables;
18|- `third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/mobilemoe.py` and `switch_layers.py`: the model code;
19|- MLX's custom-kernel documentation: `.venv/bin/python -c "import mlx.core as mx; help(mx.fast.metal_kernel)"`;
20|- `bench/grader/check_candidate.py` and `bench/grader/slots.py`: how you are graded.
21|
22|## The slots
23|
24|Each slot is a piece of the mixture-of-experts block, `MoE.__call__` in `mobilemoe.py`, which runs in all 20 layers of every step. `rows` is the number of tokens in the step: 1 to 32 in decode. The grader flattens the inputs to the shapes below and restores the model's shapes afterwards. All arrays are row-contiguous.
25|
26|The model's constants: hidden size `D = 768`, experts `E = 60`, experts per token `K = 4`, expert hidden size `H = 384`, `routed_scaling_factor = 2.5`, `norm_topk_prob = true`.
27|
28|### `routing`: router, top-4 selection and weights
29|
30|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
31||---|---|---|---|
32|| input | `x` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
33|| input | `w_router` | [60, 768] | float32 |
34|| input | `bias` | [60] | float32 (the model's bfloat16 `expert_bias`, converted exactly) |
35|| output | `inds` | [rows, 4] | uint32 |
36|| output | `weights` | [rows, 4] | float32 |
37|
38|Reference:
39|
40|```python
41|scores = mx.sigmoid(x.astype(mx.float32) @ w_router.T)          # [rows, 60]
42|inds = mx.argpartition(-(scores + bias), kth=3, axis=-1)[:, :4]  # the 4 largest biased scores
43|w = mx.take_along_axis(scores, inds, axis=-1)                    # unbiased scores of those 4
44|weights = w / (w.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True) + 1e-20) * 2.5
45|```
46|
47|The order of the 4 experts within a row is free, as long as `weights[r, j]` belongs to `inds[r, j]`. Today this slot is about 12 kernels per layer, 240 per step. It costs 1.02 ms of a 4.75 ms step at 1 request and 1.68 ms at 32 requests.
48|
49|### `combine`: weighting the routed experts' outputs and adding the shared expert
50|
51|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
52||---|---|---|---|
53|| input | `y` | [rows, 4, 768] | bfloat16 (the 4 experts' outputs, in `inds` order) |
54|| input | `weights` | [rows, 4] | float32 |
55|| input | `shared` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 (the shared expert's output) |
56|| output | `out` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
57|
58|Reference:
59|
60|```python
61|out = (y * weights[..., None]).sum(axis=-2).astype(mx.bfloat16) + shared
62|```
63|
64|Today this slot is 5 kernels per layer, 100 per step. It costs 0.61 ms at 1 request and 0.33 ms at 32 requests.
65|
66|### `routing+combine`
67|
68|Both slots above, each with its own kernels, in one candidate.
69|
70|### `experts`: the routed experts' three quantized products
71|
72|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
73||---|---|---|---|
74|| input | `x` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
75|| input | `inds` | [rows, 4] | uint32 |
76|| input | `gate_w`, `up_w` | [60, 768, 48] | uint32 (4-bit weights in [expert, in, out] layout, 8 per word along out) |
77|| input | `gate_scales`, `gate_biases`, `up_scales`, `up_biases` | [60, 768, 12] | bfloat16 (one scale and bias per 32 outputs) |
78|| input | `down_w` | [60, 384, 96] | uint32 |
79|| input | `down_scales`, `down_biases` | [60, 384, 24] | bfloat16 |
80|| output | `y` | [rows, 4, 768] | bfloat16 |
81|
82|Each weight is `w = scale * q + bias`, with `q` the 4-bit value. In MLX's affine quantization, the value for output column `o` sits in word `o / 8` at bits `4 * (o % 8)`.
83|
84|Reference: for each row `r` and each `j`, with `e = inds[r, j]`:
85|
86|```python
87|y[r, j] = (silu(x[r] @ Wgate[e]) * (x[r] @ Wup[e])) @ Wdown[e]
88|```
89|
90|As in MLX's `gather_qmm(..., transpose=False)`, each product accumulates in float32 and rounds its output to bfloat16. `silu(gate) * up` is computed on those bfloat16 values, and its result is rounded to bfloat16 before the down product.
91|
92|Today this slot is 7 kernels per layer at 1 request and 13 at 32 requests (from 16 rows, MLX also sorts the pairs by expert). It costs 0.92 ms at 1 request and 14.67 ms of a 28.19 ms step at 32 requests, half the step. It reads each expert once per (token, expert) pair.
93|
94|## Tools and limits
95|
96|- **Only `mx.fast.metal_kernel`, MLX 0.32.4.** You write the Metal body; MLX generates the signature. Inputs arrive as `const device T* name` and outputs as `device T* name`. 179|The pass criteria are the same as in the API-stage brief and were fixed before this session, as written here.
180|
181|1. **G1, runs.** It compiles and runs on real inputs at 1, 8 and 32 rows.
182|2. **G2, correct.** It is tested on inputs captured from all 20 layers during a real decode step, at 1, 8 and 32 rows.
183|   - **`routing`:** each row selects the same 4 experts. The only exception is a row whose 4th and 5th biased scores in the reference are within 1e-6 of each other; such rows are counted and reported. The weights, matched by expert, are within 1e-4 relative.

Source: `third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/mobilemoe.py:217-232` and the split harness `bench/grader/slots.py:105-119`.

- **Before (1), the experts call:** `y = self.experts(x, inds)` (`mobilemoe.py:230`) produces `y` in `inds` order (brief:53). Reference values are non-negative and sum to 2.5 per row, but a fused end-to-end model may feed anything finite — the kernel must treat `weights` as arbitrary finite float32.
- **Before (3), the shared expert:** `self.shared_expert(x)` (`mobilemoe.py:232`), a dense int4 `MLP(dim=768, hidden=1536)` (`mobilemoe.py:215,131-139`), computed on the same `x` as the routed path, outside all slots — a slot kernel may not change it.
- **After:** the residual add `h + feed_forward(...)` in `DecoderLayer.__call__` (`mobilemoe.py:258`), a bf16 add on `[rows,1,768]`, then the next layer. It expects `out` exactly as the reference value below, within G2.

Checklist (per `tracking.md`) for each neighbour:

- **Producer `SwitchGLU(x, inds)`.** Callers: `MoE.__call__` (`mobilemoe.py:230`). Callees: `gather_qmm` per product plus internal sort/unsort from rows ≥ 16 (`switch_layers.py:176-199`) — all upstream of the slot. Data: `y` [rows,4,768] bf16. Neighbours: routing before it; this slot after. Cost: the experts slot (hyp-1), untouched. Invariants: positional pairing — column `j` of `y` pairs with `weights[j]` as given; the slot must not re-sort or re-pick experts.
- **Producer routing-weights chain.** Callers: `MoE.__call__` (`mobilemoe.py:226-228`). Callees: none into the slot — it only supplies `weights`. Data: `weights` [rows,4] f32. Neighbours: top-4 selection before (untouched). Cost: the routing slot (hyp-2, ready), untouched. Invariants: no range assumption beyond finite float32.
- **Producer shared-expert MLP.** Callers: `MoE.__call__` (`mobilemoe.py:232`). Callees: 3 quantized matmuls + one fused silu-mul (`tables.md:141-144`: 4 kernels/layer, 80/step). Data: `shared` [rows,768] bf16. Neighbours: inside the slot boundary as input, outside all slots as computation. Cost: knock-out 0.51 ms @1, 2.90 ms @32 (`step-breakdown.md:172,213`), untouched. Invariants: bf16 values; the slot reads them as-is.
- **Consumer residual add.** Callers: `DecoderLayer.__call__` (`mobilemoe.py:258`). Callees: none (plain bf16 add). Data: `out` [rows,768] bf16. Neighbours: next layer's input_norm after. Cost: outside the slot. Invariants: `out` bit-compatible with the reference within G2 — the residual add amplifies nothing, but end-to-end greedy tokens (brief:185) feel any drift.

### What must stay identical

- **Rounding points:** the reference (`slots.py:51-52`, brief:61) casts `y` bf16→fp32 (exact), multiplies by the fp32 weights and sums the 4 terms in fp32, rounds the sum once to bf16 (the `.astype`), then adds `shared` in bf16. Today that is 5 kernels/layer: `copy_v`, broadcast `binary_g` multiply, strided-small `col_reduce_small` sum, `copy_v`, `binary_vv` add (`territory-other-kernels.md` checklist G, `tables.md:140`). The two bf16 roundings — the astype and the add — are the contract: a kernel that merges them (e.g. adding `shared` in fp32 and rounding once) changes the reference arithmetic and is acceptable only if every element still lands within 2 bf16 ULP at every row count and every input. Boundary checks will probe any such move beyond the captured inputs.
- **Tie rule:** no selection happens in this slot, so the 4th/5th within-1e-6 tie freedom (brief:183) belongs to routing only. Combine must pair `weights[r,j]` with `y[r,j,:]` strictly positionally — no re-sorting, re-picking, or re-normalizing experts.
- **Allowed reorderings:** the summation order of the 4 (row, j) products per output element is free within the 2-ULP tolerance, as is any thread/layout decomposition. Nothing else may move: shapes, dtypes, the fp32 accumulation, the single astype before `+ shared`, and the positional `weights[j]` ↔ `y[j]` pairing all stay.

### What the grader checks, and what it can't see

- **G1** compiles the Metal and runs it on the captured inputs at 1, 8 and 32 rows (brief:181, `check_candidate.py:206`).
- **G2 combine** checks exact shape [rows,768] and bf16 dtype, and every element within 2 bf16 ULP of the reference with the ULP floored at |r| = 0.001 (`check_candidate.py:44-47,96-109`); `pass` iff all 20 layers pass (`check_candidate.py:133-138,192-197`). Inputs are captured from all 20 layers of one real decode step per row count (`slots.py:137-171`). In a `routing+combine` candidate each part is checked on its own and combine receives the captured reference weights, never the candidate's (brief:171, `check_candidate.py:96-98,181-187`). Piece timing (median of 30 × all-20-layers eval ÷ 20) must beat `mx.compile(ref_combine)` at all three row counts to stop the slot (brief:193,195, `check_candidate.py:209-226`).
- **What it can't see:** row counts other than 1, 8 and 32 — a decode step can have any row count from 1 to 32 (brief:24); inputs other than the captured ones (other prompts, later decode steps, non-reference weights from a fused routing kernel); threadgroup-memory use near the 32 KB limit (`slots.build` enforces only the 1024-thread cap, `slots.py:275`); results that depend on thread timing; the end-to-end greedy-token check (24 tokens at 1 and 32 requests, plain MLX and vLLM) and G3 full-step timing, which the team runs after merging (brief:185-186,195). Boundary checks will probe exactly these.

### The GPU limits

At most 1,024 threads per threadgroup and 32 KB of threadgroup memory (brief:98); `grid` counts threads, not threadgroups (brief:175). Hardware: Apple M1 Pro, 16 cores, SIMD width 32, `bfloat` available in Metal (brief:99)."}

49|

51|- **Tie rule:** no selection happens in this slot, so the 4th/5th within-1e-6 tie freedom (brief:183) belongs to routing only. Combine must pair `weights[r,j]` with `y[r,j,:]` strictly positionally — no re-sorting, re-picking, or re-normalizing experts.

1|# Brief for the Muse Spark agent: write a faster MobileMoE-S decode kernel
2|
3|*Written by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5), directed by surucuonur. Committed and tagged `agent-era` before the Muse Spark session started. [Who made what](../PROVENANCE.md).*

9|Meta's MobileMoE-S, int4, is served on an Apple M1 Pro (16-core GPU, 200 GB/s, 16 GB) by vLLM through vllm-metal, which runs the model with MLX. The findings below measure where each decode step's time goes. A step is about 870–1,090 small GPU kernels and is far from both the bandwidth and compute limits. The findings name the pieces that cost the most.

11|1. **Choose.** Read the findings and choose one or two of the slots below to replace with your own fused Metal kernels. Write `muse-spark/strategy.md`: why, your design, and what each saves per step at 1 and 32 requests (your estimate). End it with the JSON block described under *Your files*. Commit it.
12|2. **Write and check.** For each chosen slot, write the kernels as files, run the grader on them, read its verdict, and improve. Up to **5 attempts per slot**; an attempt is a folder you graded and committed.
13|3. **Finish.** Write `muse-spark/summary.md`: your final attempt per slot and what you learned. Commit it.

15|**Read these first** (all in your worktree):
16|- `claude/findings/bottleneck-explained.md` and `claude/findings/step-breakdown.md`: the measured findings;
17|- `results/runs/2026-11-01-breakdown/tables.md` and `results/runs/2026-11-02-gpu-counters/tables.md`: the raw tables;

21|
22|## The slots
23|
24|Each slot is a piece of the mixture-of-experts block, `MoE.__call__` in `mobilemoe.py`, which runs in all 20 layers of every step. `rows` is the number of tokens in the step: 1 to 32 in decode. The grader flattens the inputs to the shapes below and restores the model's shapes afterwards. All arrays are row-contiguous.
25|
26|The model's constants: hidden size `D = 768`, experts `E = 60`, experts per token `K = 4`, expert hidden size `H = 384`, `routed_scaling_factor = 2.5`, `norm_topk_prob = true`.
27|
28|### `routing`: router, top-4 selection and weights
29|
30|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
31||---|---|---|---|
32|| input | `x` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
33|| input | `w_router` | [60, 768] | float32 |
34|| input | `bias` | [60] | float32 (the model's bfloat16 `expert_bias`, converted exactly) |
35|| output | `inds` | [rows, 4] | uint32 |
36|| output | `weights` | [rows, 4] | float32 |
37|
38|Reference:
39|
40|```python
41|scores = mx.sigmoid(x.astype(mx.float32) @ w_router.T)          # [rows, 60]
42|inds = mx.argpartition(-(scores + bias), kth=3, axis=-1)[:, :4]  # the 4 largest biased scores
43|w = mx.take_along_axis(scores, inds, axis=-1)                    # unbiased scores of those 4
44|weights = w / (w.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True) + 1e-20) * 2.5
45|```
46|
47|The order of the 4 experts within a row is free, as long as `weights[r, j]` belongs to `inds[r, j]`. Today this slot is about 12 kernels per layer, 240 per step. It costs 1.02 ms of a 4.75 ms step at 1 request and 1.68 ms at 32 requests.
48|
49|### `combine`: weighting the routed experts' outputs and adding the shared expert
50|
51|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
52||---|---|---|---|
53|| input | `y` | [rows, 4, 768] | bfloat16 (the 4 experts' outputs, in `inds` order) |
54|| input | `weights` | [rows, 4] | float32 |
55|| input | `shared` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 (the shared expert's output) |
56|| output | `out` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
57|
58|Reference:
59|
60|```python
61|out = (y * weights[..., None]).sum(axis=-2).astype(mx.bfloat16) + shared
62|```
63|
64|Today this slot is 5 kernels per layer, 100 per step. It costs 0.61 ms at 1 request and 0.33 ms at 32 requests.
65|
66|### `routing+combine`
67|
68|Both slots above, each with its own kernels, in one candidate.
69|
70|### `experts`: the routed experts' three quantized products
71|
72|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
73||---|---|---|---|
74|| input | `x` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
75|| input | `inds` | [rows, 4] | uint32 |
76|| input | `gate_w`, `up_w` | [60, 768, 48] | uint32 (4-bit weights in [expert, in, out] layout, 8 per word along out) |
77|| input | `gate_scales`, `gate_biases`, `up_scales`, `up_biases` | [60, 768, 12] | bfloat16 (one scale and bias per 32 outputs) |
78|| input | `down_w` | [60, 384, 96] | uint32 |
79|| input | `down_scales`, `down_biases` | [60, 384, 24] | bfloat16 |
80|| output | `y` | [rows, 4, 768] | bfloat16 |
81|
82|Each weight is `w = scale * q + bias`, with `q` the 4-bit value. In MLX's affine quantization, the value for output column `o` sits in word `o / 8` at bits `4 * (o % 8)`.
83|
84|Reference: for each row `r` and each `j`, with `e = inds[r, j]`:
85|
86|```python
87|y[r, j] = (silu(x[r] @ Wgate[e]) * (x[r] @ Wup[e])) @ Wdown[e]
88|```
89|
90|As in MLX's `gather_qmm(..., transpose=False)`, each product accumulates in float32 and rounds its output to bfloat16. `silu(gate) * up` is computed on those bfloat16 values, and its result is rounded to bfloat16 before the down product.
91|
92|Today this slot is 7 kernels per layer at 1 request and 13 at 32 requests (from 16 rows, MLX also sorts the pairs by expert). It costs 0.92 ms at 1 request and 14.67 ms of a 28.19 ms step at 32 requests, half the step. It reads each expert once per (token, expert) pair.

94|## Tools and limits
95|

def dim(expr, rows):
    if isinstance(expr, bool) or not isinstance(expr, (int, str)):
        raise ValueError(f"bad size {expr!r}")
    if isinstance(expr, int):
        return expr
    value = 1
    for term in expr.replace(" ", "").split("*"):
        if not TERM.match(term):
            raise ValueError(f"bad size term {term!r} in {expr!r}")
        value *= rows if term == "rows" else NAMES.get(term) or int(term)
    return value


def template_value(v):
    if isinstance(v, bool) or isinstance(v, int):
        return v
    if isinstance(v, str) and v in DTYPES:
        return DTYPES[v]
    raise ValueError(f"bad template value {v!r}")


def build(spec, sources, slot):
    """A function slot_inputs -> slot_outputs from Muse Spark's spec and Metal blocks."""
    slot_in, slot_out = SLOTS[slot]
    kernels = []
    for k in spec["kernels"]:
        header = "" if k.get("header_block") is None else sources[k["header_block"]]
        fn = mx.fast.metal_kernel(
            name=re.sub(r"\W", "_", str(k["name"])),
            input_names=list(k["inputs"]),
            output_names=[o["name"] for o in k["outputs"]],
            source=sources[k["source_block"]],
            header=header,
            atomic_outputs=bool(k.get("atomic_outputs", False)),
        )
        kernels.append((k, fn))
    missing = set(slot_out) - set(spec["slot_outputs"])
    if missing:
        raise ValueError(f"slot_outputs is missing {sorted(missing)}")

    def run(**inputs):
        rows = inputs[slot_in[0]].shape[0]
        env = dict(inputs)
        for k, fn in kernels:
            tg = [int(t) for t in k["threadgroup"]]
            if any(t < 1 for t in tg) or tg[0] * tg[1] * tg[2] > 1024:
                raise ValueError(f"bad threadgroup {tg}")
            outs = fn(
                inputs=[env[n] for n in k["inputs"]],
                template=[
                    (n, template_value(v)) for n, v in (k.get("template") or {}).items()
                ],
                grid=tuple(dim(g, rows) for g in k["grid"]),
                threadgroup=tuple(tg),
                output_shapes=[
                    tuple(dim(s, rows) for s in o["shape"]) for o in k["outputs"]
                ],
                output_dtypes=[DTYPES[o["dtype"]] for o in k["outputs"]],
                init_value=k.get("init_value"),
            )
            env.update(zip([o["name"] for o in k["outputs"]], outs))
        return {name: env[src] for name, src in spec["slot_outputs"].items()}

    return run

22|## The slots
23|
24|Each slot is a piece of the mixture-of-experts block, `MoE.__call__` in `mobilemoe.py`, which runs in all 20 layers of every step. `rows` is the number of tokens in the step: 1 to 32 in decode. The grader flattens the inputs to the shapes below and restores the model's shapes afterwards. All arrays are row-contiguous.
25|
26|The model's constants: hidden size `D = 768`, experts `E = 60`, experts per token `K = 4`, expert hidden size `H = 384`, `routed_scaling_factor = 2.5`, `norm_topk_prob = true`.
27|
28|### `routing`: router, top-4 selection and weights
29|
30|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
31||---|---|---|---|
32|| input | `x` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
33|| input | `w_router` | [60, 768] | float32 |
34|| input | `bias` | [60] | float32 (the model's bfloat16 `expert_bias`, converted exactly) |
35|| output | `inds` | [rows, 4] | uint32 |
36|| output | `weights` | [rows, 4] | float32 |
37|
38|Reference:
39|
40|```python
41|scores = mx.sigmoid(x.astype(mx.float32) @ w_router.T)          # [rows, 60]
42|inds = mx.argpartition(-(scores + bias), kth=3, axis=-1)[:, :4]  # the 4 largest biased scores
43|w = mx.take_along_axis(scores, inds, axis=-1)                    # unbiased scores of those 4
44|weights = w / (w.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True) + 1e-20) * 2.5
45|```
46|
47|The order of the 4 experts within a row is free, as long as `weights[r, j]` belongs to `inds[r, j]`. Today this slot is about 12 kernels per layer, 240 per step. It costs 1.02 ms of a 4.75 ms step at 1 request and 1.68 ms at 32 requests.
48|
49|### `combine`: weighting the routed experts' outputs and adding the shared expert
50|
51|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
52||---|---|---|---|
53|| input | `y` | [rows, 4, 768] | bfloat16 (the 4 experts' outputs, in `inds` order) |
54|| input | `weights` | [rows, 4] | float32 |
55|| input | `shared` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 (the shared expert's output) |
56|| output | `out` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
57|
58|Reference:
59|
60|```python
61|out = (y * weights[..., None]).sum(axis=-2).astype(mx.bfloat16) + shared
62|```
63|
64|Today this slot is 5 kernels per layer, 100 per step. It costs 0.61 ms at 1 request and 0.33 ms at 32 requests.
65|
66|### `routing+combine`
67|
68|Both slots above, each with its own kernels, in one candidate.
69|
70|### `experts`: the routed experts' three quantized products
71|
72|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
73||---|---|---|---|
74|| input | `x` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
75|| input | `inds` | [rows, 4] | uint32 |
76|| input | `gate_w`, `up_w` | [60, 768, 48] | uint32 (4-bit weights in [expert, in, out] layout, 8 per word along out) |
77|| input | `gate_scales`, `gate_biases`, `up_scales`, `up_biases` | [60, 768, 12] | bfloat16 (one scale and bias per 32 outputs) |
78|| input | `down_w` | [60, 384, 96] | uint32 |
79|| input | `down_scales`, `down_biases` | [60, 384, 24] | bfloat16 |
80|| output | `y` | [rows, 4, 768] | bfloat16 |
81|
82|Each weight is `w = scale * q + bias`, with `q` the 4-bit value. In MLX's affine quantization, the value for output column `o` sits in word `o / 8` at bits `4 * (o % 8)`.
83|
84|Reference: for each row `r` and each `j`, with `e = inds[r, j]`:
85|
86|```python
87|y[r, j] = (silu(x[r] @ Wgate[e]) * (x[r] @ Wup[e])) @ Wdown[e]
88|```
89|
90|As in MLX's `gather_qmm(..., transpose=False)`, each product accumulates in float32 and rounds its output to bfloat16. `silu(gate) * up` is computed on those bfloat16 values, and its result is rounded to bfloat16 before the down product.
91|
92|Today this slot is 7 kernels per layer at 1 request and 13 at 32 requests (from 16 rows, MLX also sorts the pairs by expert). It costs 0.92 ms at 1 request and 14.67 ms of a 28.19 ms step at 32 requests, half the step. It reads each expert once per (token, expert) pair.

82|    return y.squeeze(-2)

85|REFERENCE = {"routing": ref_routing, "combine": ref_combine, "experts": ref_experts}

88|def expert_weights(experts):
89|    """A layer's SwitchGLU weights, named as in the experts slot."""
90|    return {
91|        f"{p}_{t}": getattr(experts, f"{p}_proj")[k]
92|        for p in ("gate", "up", "down")
93|        for t, k in (("w", "weight"), ("scales", "scales"), ("biases", "biases"))
94|    }

97|def make_moe_call(routing=ref_routing, combine=ref_combine, experts=None):
98|    """MoE.__call__ with its slots swapped for *routing*, *combine*, *experts*.
99|
100|    With the references it gives the port's outputs bit for bit (checked by
101|    check_identity), so any difference comes from the swapped slot. With
102|    experts=None the port's own SwitchGLU runs.
103|    """
104|
105|    def moe_call(self, x):
106|        lead = x.shape[:-1]
107|        flat = x.reshape(-1, D)
108|        bias = self.expert_bias.astype(mx.float32)
109|        inds, weights = routing(flat, self.router.weight, bias)
110|        if experts is None:
111|            y = self.experts(x, inds.reshape(*lead, K))
112|        else:
113|            w = expert_weights(self.experts)
114|            y = experts(flat, inds, *[w[n] for n in EXPERT_WEIGHTS])
115|        shared = self.shared_expert(x)
116|        out = combine(y.reshape(-1, K, D), weights, shared.reshape(-1, D))
117|        return out.reshape(*lead, D)
118|
119|    return moe_call

122|def check_identity(model):
123|    """The split MoE with reference slots equals the port's, at 1, 8, 32 rows."""
124|    from mlx_lm.models import mobilemoe
125|
126|    original = mobilemoe.MoE.__call__
127|    for split in (make_moe_call(), make_moe_call(experts=ref_experts)):
128|        for rows in (1, 8, 32):
129|            moe = model.model.layers[3].feed_forward
130|            x = mx.random.normal((1, rows, D)).astype(mx.bfloat16)
131|            if not mx.array_equal(original(moe, x), split(moe, x)).item():
132|                raise AssertionError(
133|                    f"split MoE differs from the port's at {rows} rows"
134|                )

137|def capture(model, rows, step=8, seed=None):
138|    """Every layer's slot inputs and reference outputs in one real decode step."""
139|    import sys
140|
141|    sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "micro"))
142|    import breakdown as bd
143|    from mlx_lm.models import mobilemoe
144|    from mlx_lm.models.cache import make_prompt_cache
145|
146|    original = mobilemoe.MoE.__call__
147|    seen = []
148|
149|    def recording_routing(x, w_router, bias):
150|        inds, weights = ref_routing(x, w_router, bias)
151|        seen.append({"x": x, "w_router": w_router, "bias": bias, "inds": inds})
152|        return inds, weights
153|
154|    def recording_combine(y, weights, shared):
155|        seen[-1].update(y=y, weights_in=weights, shared=shared)
156|        return ref_combine(y, weights, shared)
157|
158|    mx.random.seed(rows if seed is None else seed)
159|    ids = mx.random.randint(0, 100000, (rows, 128))
160|    cache = make_prompt_cache(model)
161|    y = bd.prefill(model, ids, cache)
162|    for _ in range(step - 1):
163|        y = bd.greedy(model(y, cache=cache))
164|        mx.eval(y)
165|    mobilemoe.MoE.__call__ = make_moe_call(recording_routing, recording_combine)
166|    try:
167|        logits = model(y, cache=cache)
168|        mx.eval(logits, [list(s.values()) for s in seen])
169|    finally:
170|        mobilemoe.MoE.__call__ = original
171|    return seen
172|
173|
174|def save_inputs(model):
175|    INPUTS.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
176|    for rows in (1, 8, 32):
177|        layers = capture(model, rows)
178|        arrays = {
179|            f"L{i:02d}_{k}": np.array(
180|                v.astype(mx.float32) if v.dtype == mx.bfloat16 else v
181|            )
182|            for i, layer in enumerate(layers)
183|            for k, v in layer.items()
184|        }
185|        np.savez(INPUTS / f"rows{rows}.npz", **arrays)
186|        print(f"captured {len(layers)} layers at {rows} rows", flush=True)

189|def load_expert_weights():
190|    """Every layer's SwitchGLU weights, from the served checkpoint."""
191|    import sys
192|
193|    sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "micro"))
194|    import breakdown as bd
195|    from mlx_lm.utils import load_model
196|
197|    model, _ = load_model(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / bd.MODEL)
198|    weights = [
199|        expert_weights(layer.feed_forward.experts) for layer in model.model.layers
200|    ]
201|    mx.eval(weights)
202|    return weights

204|
205|def load_inputs(rows, with_weights=None):
206|    """[{name: mx.array}] per layer, with bfloat16 restored where the model had it.
207|
208|    *with_weights*, from load_expert_weights, adds each layer's expert weights.
209|    """
210|    data = np.load(INPUTS / f"rows{rows}.npz")
211|    bf16 = {"x", "y", "shared"}
212|    layers = {}
213|    for key in data.files:
214|        i, name = int(key[1:3]), key[4:]
215|        a = mx.array(data[key])
216|        layers.setdefault(i, {})[name] = a.astype(mx.bfloat16) if name in bf16 else a
217|    for i, layer in layers.items():
218|        layer["weights"] = layer.pop("weights_in")
219|        if "inds" in layer:
220|            layer["inds"] = layer["inds"].astype(mx.uint32)
221|        if with_weights is not None:
222|            layer.update(with_weights[i])
223|    return [layers[i] for i in sorted(layers)]

226|# Muse Spark's launch spec: integers, or products of integers and NAMES/rows.
227|TERM = re.compile(r"^(\d+|rows|D|E|K|H)$")
228|
229|
230|def dim(expr, rows):
231|    if isinstance(expr, bool) or not isinstance(expr, (int, str)):
232|        raise ValueError(f"bad size {expr!r}")
233|    if isinstance(expr, int):
234|        return expr
235|    value = 1
236|    for term in expr.replace(" ", "").split("*"):
237|        if not TERM.match(term):
238|            raise ValueError(f"bad size term {term!r} in {expr!r}")
239|        value *= rows if term == "rows" else NAMES.get(term) or int(term)
240|    return value
241|
242|
243|def template_value(v):
244|    if isinstance(v, bool) or isinstance(v, int):
245|        return v
246|    if isinstance(v, str) and v in DTYPES:
247|        return DTYPES[v]
248|    raise ValueError(f"bad template value {v!r}")
249|
250|
251|def build(spec, sources, slot):
252|    """A function slot_inputs -> slot_outputs from Muse Spark's spec and Metal blocks."""
253|    slot_in, slot_out = SLOTS[slot]
254|    kernels = []
255|    for k in spec["kernels"]:
256|        header = "" if k.get("header_block") is None else sources[k["header_block"]]
257|        fn = mx.fast.metal_kernel(
258|            name=re.sub(r"\W", "_", str(k["name"])),
259|            input_names=list(k["inputs"]),
260|            output_names=[o["name"] for o in k["outputs"]],
261|            source=sources[k["source_block"]],
262|            header=header,
263|            atomic_outputs=bool(k.get("atomic_outputs", False)),
264|        )
265|        kernels.append((k, fn))
266|    missing = set(slot_out) - set(spec["slot_outputs"])
267|    if missing:
268|        raise ValueError(f"slot_outputs is missing {sorted(missing)}")
269|
270|    def run(**inputs):
271|        rows = inputs[slot_in[0]].shape[0]
272|        env = dict(inputs)
273|        for k, fn in kernels:
274|            tg = [int(t) for t in k["threadgroup"]]
275|            if any(t < 1 for t in tg) or tg[0] * tg[1] * tg[2] > 1024:
276|                raise ValueError(f"bad threadgroup {tg}")
277|            outs = fn(
278|                inputs=[env[n] for n in k["inputs"]],
279|                template=[
280|                    (n, template_value(v)) for n, v in (k.get("template") or {}).items()
281|                ],
282|                grid=tuple(dim(g, rows) for g in k["grid"]),
283|                threadgroup=tuple(tg),
284|                output_shapes=[
285|                    tuple(dim(s, rows) for s in o["shape"]) for o in k["outputs"]
286|                ],
287|                output_dtypes=[DTYPES[o["dtype"]] for o in k["outputs"]],
288|                init_value=k.get("init_value"),
289|            )
290|            env.update(zip([o["name"] for o in k["outputs"]], outs))
291|        return {name: env[src] for name, src in spec["slot_outputs"].items()}
292|
293|    return run
294|
295|
296|def main():
297|    import sys
298|
299|    if sys.argv[1:] != ["capture"]:
300|        raise SystemExit("usage: slots.py capture")
301|    sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "micro"))
302|    import breakdown as bd
303|    import gpu_lock
304|
305|    gpu_lock.hold("slots.py capture")
306|    from mlx_lm.utils import load_model
307|
308|    model, _ = load_model(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / bd.MODEL)
309|    mx.eval(model.parameters())
310|    check_identity(model)
311|    print("split MoE with reference slots: bit-identical to the port's")
312|    save_inputs(model)
313|
314|
315|if __name__ == "__main__":
316|    main()

1|"""Grade one kernel attempt: compile it, test it on captured inputs, time it.
2|
3|The independent grader for Muse Spark's kernels (claude/muse-agent-brief.md).
4|It runs on the inputs `slots.py capture` recorded from a real decode step,
5|prints its verdict as JSON, and writes it to --out when given. It never
6|writes into the attempt folder, which holds only Muse Spark's files.

8|  .venv/bin/python bench/grader/check_candidate.py muse-spark/kernels/<slot>/attempt-N <slot> [--out FILE]
9|"""

44|def ulp_bf16(r):
45|    """bfloat16's unit in the last place at |r|, floored at |r| = 0.001 (brief, G2)."""
46|    exp = np.floor(np.log2(np.maximum(np.abs(r), 1e-3)))
47|    return 2.0 ** (exp - 7)

52|    got = fn(x=layer["x"], w_router=layer["w_router"], bias=layer["bias"])
53|    inds, w = got["inds"], got["weights"]
54|    rows = layer["x"].shape[0]
55|    if inds.shape != (rows, slots.K) or w.shape != (rows, slots.K):

58|        }

148|        mx.eval([fn(**{n: layer[n] for n in names}) for layer in layers])

1|// Fused combine: weight the 4 experts' bf16 outputs by fp32 weights, sum in
2|// fp32, round once to bf16, add shared — one kernel launch per layer, one
3|// thread per output element. Grid is (rows*768, 1, 1), threadgroup (256, 1, 1).
4|//
5|// Reference (slots.py:51-52): (y * weights[..., None]).sum(axis=-2)
6|//   .astype(bf16) + shared. y is [rows,4,768] bf16 row-contiguous, weights
7|//   [rows,4] f32, shared [rows,768] bf16, out [rows,768] bf16. The bfloat
8|//   conversion and the + shared use the same single-rounding ops as MLX's
9|//   copy_v/binary_vv kernels, and the 4-term fp32 sum order is free per the
10|//   hyp-3 boundary.
11|
12|uint idx = thread_position_in_grid.x;
13|uint row = idx / 768u;
14|uint d = idx - row * 768u;
15|
16|uint wbase = row * 4u;
17|uint ybase = row * 3072u + d; // 4*768
18|uint sbase = row * 768u + d;
19|
20|float acc = float(y[ybase]) * weights[wbase]
21|    + float(y[ybase + 768u]) * weights[wbase + 1u]
22|    + float(y[ybase + 1536u]) * weights[wbase + 2u]
23|    + float(y[ybase + 2304u]) * weights[wbase + 3u];
24|
25|out[sbase] = bfloat(acc) + shared[sbase];

9|## Inefficiency
10|
11|Slot `experts`. One combined fix for five confirmed entries (savings do not add; joint ceiling 443 MB at streaming rate ≈ 11.5 ms at 32 rows, per the verifier):
12|
13|- `ineff-quantized-kernels-1` (rank 1, mean 19.9% of step): per-pair qvm grids at ~1/3 peak; ideal 0.5 / 2.5 / 8.6 ms at 1/8/32 rows.
14|- `ineff-findings-2` (rank 3, mean 10.4%): measured 25% grouped-kernel win; 0.40 / 1.30 / 3.67 ms.
15|- `ineff-switch-layers-2` (rank 4, mean 4.3%): unfused products+activation; ~0.4 ms at all row counts.
16|- `ineff-runs-1` (rank 6, mean 4.2%): 465 MB excess re-reads; floor 0.0 / 0.6 / 2.3 ms.
17|- `ineff-switch-layers-1` (rank 7, mean 0.8%): sort glue 0.7 ms at 32 rows, removable only inside this fix.
18|
19|Design: one Metal kernel that batches same-expert pairs with coalesced reads, runs gate/up/down plus the activation with intermediates on-chip, and needs no sort/unsort. Must keep the G2 boundary (2 bf16 ULP, fp32 accumulation, bf16 rounding points).

21|## Boundary

23|(written by boundary-1; every line carries its source)

25|### Inputs and outputs
26|
27|Sources: the brief's `experts` slot section (`claude/muse-agent-brief.md:70-92`) and `bench/grader/slots.py:19-40,271`. Constants `D,E,K,H = 768,60,4,384` (slots.py:19; brief:26). All arrays row-contiguous (brief:24). `rows` is read from the first slot input's `shape[0]` (slots.py:271); any 1–32 in decode (brief:24).

29|| Name | Shape at 1 / 8 / 32 rows | Dtype | Layout / notes |
30||---|---|---|---|
31|| `x` | [1,768] / [8,768] / [32,768] | bfloat16 | brief:74 |
32|| `inds` | [1,4] / [8,4] / [32,4] | uint32 | brief:75; cast to u32 on load, slots.py:219-220 |
33|| `gate_w`, `up_w` | [60,768,48], rows-independent | uint32 | [expert,in,out] transposed layout (brief:76; mobilemoe.py:42,202-214); 8 4-bit values per word along out; output column `o` sits in word `o/8` at bits `4*(o%8)` (brief:82) |
34|| `gate_scales`, `gate_biases`, `up_scales`, `up_biases` | [60,768,12] each, rows-independent | bfloat16 | one scale and bias per 32 outputs (brief:77); `w = scale*q + bias`, affine, group_size 32, bits 4 (brief:82; slots.py:67-77) |
35|| `down_w` | [60,384,96], rows-independent | uint32 | same packing as gate/up (brief:78) |
36|| `down_scales`, `down_biases` | [60,384,24] each, rows-independent | bfloat16 | one scale and bias per 32 outputs (brief:79) |
37|| `y` (output) | [1,4,768] / [8,4,768] / [32,4,768] | bfloat16 | brief:80; `y[r,j]` is expert `inds[r,j]`'s output, positional (see neighbour B) |

40|The spec's `slot_outputs` must provide `y` (slots.py:266-268). Grid counts threads, not threadgroups (slots.py:283).
41|
42|### Before and after
43|
44|Source: `MoE.__call__` (`third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/mobilemoe.py:217-232`) and the split MoE the grader installs (`bench/grader/slots.py:97-119`, bit-identical to the port per `check_identity`, slots.py:122-134). Order per layer: post_attention_layernorm → `x`; router → `inds`, `weights`; experts(`x`, `inds`) → `y`; shared_expert(`x`) → `shared` (independent of this slot, runs alongside); combine(`y`, `weights`, `shared`) → `out` → residual / next layer (mobilemoe.py:230-232,257-258; slots.py:105-118). The grader flattens model `[B,L,D]` to `[rows,D]` and restores shapes afterwards (brief:24; slots.py:106-117).
45|
46|Neighbour A — what produces the slot's inputs (layernorm + routing), per tracking.md checklist:
47|- **Callers:** `MoE.__call__` in all 20 layers of every decode step (mobilemoe.py:217-230; brief:24).
48|- **Callees:** router Linear in float32, sigmoid, `argpartition(-biased, kth=3)`, `take_along_axis`, normalize `+1e-20` then `×2.5` (slots.py:44-48; mobilemoe.py:219-228).
49|- **Data:** `x` is bf16 RMSNorm output, flattened [rows,768]; `inds` is u32 [rows,4], 4 distinct experts per row in arbitrary order, values in [0,60) (slots.py:44-48; routing G2 rejects inds ≥ 60, check_candidate.py:65).
50|- **Neighbours:** this slot must accept `inds` in ANY order, including either side of a routing near-tie: within-row order is free (brief:47) and routing G2 matches expert sets, skipping rows whose 4th/5th biased scores are within 1e-6 (check_candidate.py:71-80).
51|- **Cost:** routing's own ~12 kernels/layer (brief:47) — not this slot's cost.
52|- **Invariants:** `inds` valid [0,60); `x` finite bf16; row count any 1–32 (brief:24), not just 1/8/32.
53|
54|Neighbour B — what consumes `y` (combine + residual), per tracking.md checklist:
55|- **Callers:** combine is called as `combine(y.reshape(-1,K,D), weights, shared.reshape(-1,D))` (slots.py:116).
56|- **Callees:** `(y * weights[...,None]).sum(axis=-2).astype(bf16) + shared` (slots.py:51-52; mobilemoe.py:231-232).
57|- **Data:** `y` [rows,4,768] bf16 "in `inds` order" (brief:53); `weights` [rows,4] f32; `shared` [rows,768] bf16; `out` [rows,768] bf16 → reshaped to lead dims, added to the residual, fed to the next layer (slots.py:116-117).
58|- **Neighbours:** combine pairs `y[...,j,:]` with `weights[...,j]` POSITIONALLY (slots.py:52), so `y[r,j]` MUST be the output of expert `inds[r,j]` — no reordering of the K axis is visible downstream. Slot-edge traffic floor: `y` (rows·6144 B per layer) is written here and re-read by combine; ≈0.04 ms/step at 32 rows, unremovable within the interface (`territory-grader.md`, Boundary floor).
59|- **Cost:** combine's own 5 kernels/layer (brief:64) — not this slot's cost.
60|- **Invariants:** `y` must have the exact shape and bf16 dtype or G2 fails (check_candidate.py:117-118).
61|
62|### What must stay identical
63|
64|- **Reference math:** for each row `r` and `j`, with `e = inds[r,j]`: `y[r,j] = (silu(x[r] @ Wgate[e]) * (x[r] @ Wup[e])) @ Wdown[e]` (brief:84-88); port code `ref_experts` (slots.py:55-82) with `swiglu(gate,x) = silu(gate)*x` (activations.py:9-11), `gather_qmm(..., transpose=False, group_size=32, bits=4, mode="affine")` (slots.py:67-77).
65|- **Rounding points:** each gate/up/down product accumulates in float32 and rounds its output to bfloat16; `silu(gate)*up` is computed on those bfloat16 values and rounded to bfloat16 before the down product (brief:90). Keep fp32 accumulation (nothing narrower) and all four bf16 rounding points (carry no wider precision across them) — this hypothesis's stated G2 boundary.
66|- **Tie rule:** there is NONE inside this slot — instead the slot inherits routing's freedom: it must handle any 4 valid expert ids per row in any order, never assuming sorted `inds` or the reference `argpartition` order (brief:47; check_candidate.py:71-80).
67|- **Allowed reorderings:** any summation order inside fp32 accumulation; any grouping of (row, expert) pairs and any thread/block decomposition; sort or no sort at ANY row count including ≥16 (the reference sorts iff `inds.size >= 64`, slots.py:62, switch_layers.py:181, but G2 compares outputs only, so the choice is free — `territory-grader.md` note on ineff-runs-3); any dequantization order. **Forbidden:** moving any `y` element off its `[r,j,d]` position, changing shapes/dtypes, narrowing accumulation below fp32, skipping a bf16 rounding, or fusing across the slot edges (`x`/`inds` in, `y` out stay in DRAM between slots).
68|
69|### What the grader checks, and what it can't see
70|
71|Checks (`bench/grader/check_candidate.py`):
72|- **G1:** compiles and runs on real inputs at 1, 8 and 32 rows (`g1=True` after the loops, 206; any exception → error + g1 false, 227-228, Metal errors trimmed by `short_error`, 153-163). Note: shape/dtype mismatches are per-layer stats, not exceptions — they fail G2 with g1 true (188-191).
73|- **G2 experts** (`check_experts`, 112-130): exact shape [rows,4,768] and bf16 dtype (117-118); EVERY element within 2 bf16 ULP of the reference, with the ULP floored at |r| = 0.001 so reorderings near zero don't fail (`ulp_bf16`, 44-47; 119-123). All 20 layers' captured inputs at each of 1/8/32 rows must pass (179-205). Inputs are seeded (`mx.random.seed(rows)`, slots.py:158) — deterministic every run.
74|- **Piece timing** runs only if G2 passes (209-226): median of 30 repeats of all-20-layer evals, per layer; `beats_compiled` needs candidate < compiled reference at ALL three row counts. "It is a guide; G3 decides" (brief:193).
75|What it can't see (checked by hand later — boundary.md *check an attempt*):
76|- Row counts other than 1, 8 and 32: any 1–32 occur in decode (brief:24); grids and indexing must be valid for all of them.
77|- Inputs beyond the captured set: one seeded run of 128-token random prompts, decode step 8 (slots.py:158-168). Real prompts, steps and activation distributions differ — no assumption fitted to the captured values survives.
78|- Reads of threadgroup memory never written, results that depend on thread timing, out-of-bounds reads that luckily pass, threadgroup memory over 32 KB (`build` enforces only the thread COUNT, slots.py:274-276, not the 32 KB).
79|- End-to-end and G3, run after merge (`time_candidates.py`): the same greedy tokens over 24 generated tokens at 1 and 32 requests in plain MLX and vLLM (brief:185), and a lower decode-step period than both the original and the compiled reference with the gap exceeding the repeat spread (brief:186).

81|### The GPU limits
82|
83|- At most 1,024 threads per threadgroup (brief:98; count enforced in slots.py:275) and 32 KB of threadgroup memory (brief:98; NOT enforced by `build` — verify by hand from the Metal source).
84|- Grid counts threads (slots.py:283); sizes are ints or products of ints and rows/D/E/K/H only (slots.py:230-240); dtypes float32/bfloat16/float16/uint32/int32 (slots.py:22-28).
85|- Only `mx.fast.metal_kernel`, MLX 0.32.4; the grader runs no Python of the candidate's — the spec is data, only the Metal compiles (brief:96-97). A grader run should take under 3 minutes (brief:98).
86|- Hardware: Apple M1 Pro GPU, 16 cores, SIMD width 32, bfloat16 as `bfloat` in Metal (brief:99).
