1|# attempt-2: fused per-pair experts (direction b)
2|
3|First in direction (b): fusion first, keeping per-pair reads. One Metal kernel,
4|one 128-thread threadgroup per (row, expert-slot) pair. Gate/up share one
5|i-loop over an on-chip x row; gate/up/hidden intermediates stay in threadgroup
6|memory (1920 bf16 = 3840 B, under the 32 KB limit); each expert's weights are
7|read once per pair with no cross-pair batching and no sort.
8|
9|Removes `ineff-switch-layers-2` (unfused products + activation): 4 on-chain
10|kernels/layer become 1, and gate/up/hidden intermediates never touch DRAM. It
11|does NOT remove `ineff-quantized-kernels-1` (per-pair re-reads of weights) or
12|`ineff-runs-1` (465 MB excess) — those are directions (a)/(c).
13|
14|Boundary kept: fp32 accumulation, bf16 rounding after each product and after
15|silu-mul, `y[r,j]` positional, any `inds` order, valid for all 1–32 rows
16|(grid is `rows*512` threads = `rows*4` pairs × 128, no rows-dependent indexing).
17|
18|## Predicted µs per layer at 1 / 8 / 32 rows
19|
20|Per-pair weight bytes (exact): each of gate/up/down is 147,456 B of `_w` +
21|18,432 B scales + 18,432 B biases = 184,320 B; ×3 = 552,960 B ≈ 553 KB
22|(agrees with ineff-quantized-kernels-1's 540 KB model). Pairs/layer: 4/32/128
23|→ 2.21 / 17.7 / 70.8 MB per layer. Rate basis: ~100 GB/s (below the 150 GB/s
24|streaming ideal — one thread's consecutive-i reads stride 48/96 words, so
25|coalescing is imperfect; but each word is read once per pair and x is on-chip,
26|unlike the reference's 12× x re-reads and strided down re-reads).
27|
28|- 1 row: 2.21 MB / 100 GB/s = 22 µs + one launch ≈ 7 µs → **30 µs**
29|  (original 46 µs/layer = 0.92 ms ÷ 20, brief:92).
30|- 8 rows: 17.7 MB / 100 = 177 µs → **185 µs**
31|  (baseline ≈254 µs/layer = 5.08 ms ÷ 20, ineff-quantized-kernels-1 micro).
32|- 32 rows: 70.8 MB × ~0.65 (128 pairs share ~20–60 distinct experts/layer, so
33|  part of the re-reads hit cache) = 46 MB / 100 = 460 µs → **470 µs**
34|  (original 733 µs/layer = 14.67 ms ÷ 20, brief:92).
35|
36|Plus the 3 saved launches/layer (3 × 6.81 µs = 20 µs, ineff-switch-layers-2)
37|are inside these numbers via the single-launch timing. beats_compiled:
38|predicted true at 1 and 8 rows; 32 rows a toss-up since per-pair bytes match
39|the reference.
40|
41|## v2: bit-faithful numerics (same attempt folder)
42|
43|v1 graded G1 pass / G2 fail: ~7% of elements over 2 ULP (max 11/32/68 ULP at
44|1/8/32 rows), all on near-zero down outputs. Cause: v1 accumulated each dot
45|serially, while the reference (`affine_gather_qvm`, quantized.h qvm_impl)
46|accumulates 32 strided per-lane partials and reduces with a `simd_sum` tree;
47|down outputs near cancellation amplify even 1-ULP hidden flips past the 2-ULP
48|floor, so gate/up/hidden must match bit-exactly. v2 replicates per output:
49|lane l sums k=l,l+32,... with qouter's exact op forms (`s/16` times the
50|unshifted high nibble for odd outputs), then a real `simd_sum` over the same
51|lane mapping; silu uses MLX's Sigmoid lowering
52|(`1/(1+precise::exp(abs(x)))`, branch on sign) in fp32, since the struct
53|cannot instantiate for bfloat. Design unchanged: same fusion, same per-pair
54|reads. Predictions unchanged: 30 / 185 / 470 µs per layer.
55|
56|v2 graded G1 pass / G2 fail with IDENTICAL failures to v1 (same bad counts,
57|same worst values to 7 digits) — proving the error is systematic, not order.
58|CPU replication (/tmp/cpu_pair.py, safetensors read directly, no GPU) matched
59|the kernel bit-for-bit and showed all fp32 summation orders agree to ~1e-9
60|while the reference differs by ~7.7e-5: the down TERMS differ, i.e. hidden.
61|Gate/up proven order-insensitive (0 bf16 flips across serial/reverse/tree).
62|A search over all 64 bf16-rounding placements in silu (/tmp/cpu_silu.py) found
63|only full-bf16 (round after exp/add/recip/sub/mul/mul) matches: bad=0 on both
64|probe pairs. So MLX's compiled swiglu computes entirely in bf16.
65|
66|## v3: bf16 silu (same attempt folder)
67|
68|v2 + per-op bf16 rounding in silu (exp/add/recip/sub/mul/mul). Design,
69|predictions unchanged: 30 / 185 / 470 µs per layer.
70|
71|## Verdict
72|
73|G1 pass; G2 pass with max_ulp 0.0 at all row counts (bit-exact vs reference);
74|beats_compiled true. Piece timing µs/layer (candidate vs original vs
75|compiled): rows 1: 107.3 / 99.8 / 135.0; rows 8: 188.4 / 218.7 / 216.9;
76|rows 32: 647.6 / 768.6 / 761.7. Beats the compiled reference at all rows
77|(~20/13/15%) and the eager original at 8/32 rows (~14/16%), but REGRESSES
78|7.5% vs eager at 1 row.
79|
80|## Miss analysis (prediction 30 / 185 / 470)
81|
82|- Rows 1 (+257%): wrong regime. 4 pairs = 512 threads is occupancy-starved
83|  (2.2 MB in 107 µs = 20 GB/s effective), not streaming at 100 GB/s. Fusion
84|  saves 3 launches but one threadgroup per pair parallelizes worse than the
85|  reference's 96 small groups here. Lesson: direction (b) cannot win at 1
86|  row; needs the grouped designs' occupancy.
87|- Rows 8 (+2%): 17.7 MB in 188 µs = 94 GB/s. Model holds.
88|- Rows 32 (+38%): streams at 109 GB/s (better than assumed) but with NO
89|  cross-pair cache reuse — effective bytes are the full 70.8 MB/layer, not
90|  the assumed 0.65×46 MB. 128 pairs × 553 KB = 70 MB >> GPU cache, and the
91|  20 sequential layer evals evict; distinct experts/layer are too many for
92|  reuse. Lesson: per-pair re-reads cost full DRAM bandwidth; only batching
93|  same-expert pairs (directions a/c, `ineff-runs-1`) removes them.

3|First attempt in this direction: one Metal kernel per layer fusing the whole
4|combine chain (bf16→fp32 cast, multiply, sum, fp32→bf16 cast, + shared). One
5|thread per output element on a rows×768 grid, threadgroup 256 (768 = 3×256,
6|so the grid is always whole threadgroups). Each thread loads its 4 bf16
7|values, converts exactly to fp32, weights, sums in fp32, rounds once with
8|`bfloat(acc)`, and adds `shared` with the same single-rounding bf16 add as
9|MLX's `binary_vv`.
10|
11|## Inefficiency removed
12|
13|`ineff-model-2`: each layer's weighting launches 5 tiny kernels (AsType,
14|Multiply, Sum, AsType, Add) costing 0.61 ms/step at 1 row for ~6 MB of
15|activations — pure launch overhead on an overhead-bound chain. This attempt
16|replaces all 5 with 1 launch/layer, keeping both bf16 rounding points of the
17|reference (`slots.py:51-52`): the astype before `+ shared`, then the bf16
18|add. The 4-term fp32 sum order is free per the hyp-3 boundary.

22|Per the hyp-2 lesson (routing attempt-1 notes), predict against the ~24
23|µs/layer fused-kernel harness floor, not 6.81 µs/launch. Traffic per layer
24|is y rows×4×768 bf16 + weights rows×4 f32 + shared rows×768 bf16 + out
25|rows×768 bf16 = rows×9232 B ≈ 9.0 KB/row; at 200 GB/s (brief:9) that is
26|0.05 / 0.4 / 1.4 µs at 1/8/32 rows — negligible next to the floor. The grid
27|holds 3 / 24 / 96 threadgroups, so amortization is at least as good as
28|routing's 8-row case (23.6 µs):
29|
30|- 1 row: 24 + 0.05 ≈ **24 µs**
31|- 8 rows: 24 + 0.4 ≈ **24 µs**
32|- 32 rows: 24 + 1.4 ≈ **25 µs**
33|

48|0.001); max ULP 0.0 / 2.0 / 1.0 at 1/8/32 rows — the 8-row case touches the

58|(28% under). The 24 µs figure was routing-specific, not a universal harness
59|floor: routing attempt-1 runs one threadgroup/row with two threadgroup
60|barriers, a 60-element serial top-4 scan on thread 0, and ~92k FLOP/row of
61|dot products — at 1 row that is a single wavefront plus a serial tail on a
62|16-core GPU. This kernel is a trivially parallel streaming op (~12 FLOP per

29|amortization is worse. Take a 21 µs floor at 1 row, 19 µs at 8/32 rows.

{"content":""""boundary-3 probe: can the 4-term fp32 sum order fail G2 on non-captured inputs?

Pure-numpy CPU emulation (no GPU, no model). Both attempts compute the same
left-leaning order ((p0+p1)+p2)+p3 in fp32; MLX v0.32.4 col_reduce_small
computes op(new, totals) = new + totals, i.e. right-leaning p3+(p2+(p1+p0))
when each of the 4 reduced elements lands on its own lid.y thread
(group (32,4,1) per territory-other-kernels.md:111-113), or a split-2 variant
if dispatch picks lsize.y=2. We compare the candidate order against every
plausible reference association and score with the exact G2 metric from
bench/grader/check_candidate.py:44-47,96-109 (bad iff > 2 ULP, floor 0.001).
"""
import numpy as np

F32 = np.float32

def to_bf16_f32(a):
    """RNE float32 -> bf16, returned as float32 holding exact bf16 values."""
    u = np.asarray(a, dtype=F32).view(np.uint32)
    lsb = (u >> np.uint32(16)) & np.uint32(1)
    u = u + (np.uint32(0x7FFF) + lsb)
    return ((u >> np.uint32(16)).astype(np.uint32) << np.uint32(16)).view(F32)

def ulp_bf16(r):
    exp = np.floor(np.log2(np.maximum(np.abs(r), 1e-3)))
    return 2.0 ** (exp - 7)

def g2_ulp(g, r):
    with np.errstate(over="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
        over = np.nan_to_num(np.abs(g - r) / ulp_bf16(r), nan=1e9, posinf=1e9)
    return over

def prods(y, w):
    # y: [N,4] f32 exact-bf16, w: [N,4] f32. One rounding per product, as binary_g.
    y = y.astype(F32); w = w.astype(F32)
    return tuple((y[:, j] * w[:, j]).astype(F32) for j in range(4))

def cand_order(p):
    # ((p0+p1)+p2)+p3 — attempt-1's a+b+c+d and attempt-2's acc loop (0+p0 exact).
    return (((p[0] + p[1]).astype(F32) + p[2]).astype(F32) + p[3]).astype(F32)

def ref_right(p):
    # p3+(p2+(p1+p0)) — col_reduce_small lsize.y=4, one element/thread.
    t = (p[1] + p[0]).astype(F32); t = (p[2] + t).astype(F32); return (p[3] + t).astype(F32)

def ref_split2(p):
    # thread0: p2+p0; thread1: p3+p1; combine (p3+p1)+(p2+p0) — lsize.y=2.
    t0 = (p[2] + p[0]).astype(F32); t1 = (p[3] + p[1]).astype(F32)
    return (t1 + t0).astype(F32)

def ref_pair(p):
    return ((p[0] + p[1]).astype(F32) + (p[2] + p[3]).astype(F32)).astype(F32)

def ref_left0(p):
    # (((0+p0)+p1)+p2)+p3 — sequential init-0 loop (attempt-2's shape, sanity).
    t = (F32(0.0) + p[0]).astype(F32)
    for j in (1, 2, 3):
        t = (t + p[j]).astype(F32)
    return t

REFS = {"right-leaning(y4)": ref_right, "split-2(y2)": ref_split2,
        "pairwise": ref_pair, "left-init0": ref_left0}

def full(acc, shared):
    # astype then bf16 add, identical op on both sides (cancels in comparison).
    a = to_bf16_f32(acc)
    return to_bf16_f32(a.astype(F32) + shared.astype(F32))

def score(y, w, s, tag):
    p = prods(y, w)
    g = full(cand_order(p), s)
    print(f"--- {tag}: N={y.shape[0]}", flush=True)
    for name, fn in REFS.items():
        r = full(fn(p), s)
        over = g2_ulp(g.astype(np.float64), r.astype(np.float64))
        print(f"  vs {name:16s} max_ulp={over.max():8.3f} bad(>2)={int((over > 2).sum())}", flush=True)
    return g

rng = np.random.default_rng(0)

# 1) Captured inputs: validate emulation against the grader's 0.0/2.0/1.0.
for f in ("rows1", "rows8", "rows32"):
    z = np.load(f"models/muse-inputs/{f}.npz")
    Y = np.concatenate([np.asarray(z[f"L{i:02d}_y"]).reshape(-1, 4 * 768) for i in range(20)])
    W = np.concatenate([np.asarray(z[f"L{i:02d}_weights_in"]).reshape(-1, 4) for i in range(20)])
    S = np.concatenate([np.asarray(z[f"L{i:02d}_shared"]).reshape(-1, 768) for i in range(20)])
    R = Y.shape[0]
    y = Y.reshape(R * 768, 4).astype(F32)  # per-d expert quads
    w = np.repeat(W, 768, axis=0).astype(F32)
    s = S.reshape(R * 768).astype(F32)
    # captured y/shared came from bf16 (slots.py:179-181: bf16->f32 exact); re-quantize = identity
    assert np.array_equal(to_bf16_f32(y), y) and np.array_equal(to_bf16_f32(s), s)
    score(y, w, s, f"captured-{f} (gradr max ULP 0.0/2.0/1.0)")

# 2) Realistic synthetic fuzz, calibrated to captured stats.
N = 20_000_000
y = to_bf16_f32(rng.normal(0, 0.0042, (N, 4)))
w = (rng.dirichlet(np.ones(4), N) * 2.5).astype(F32)
s = to_bf16_f32(rng.normal(0, 0.022, N))
score(y, w, s, "realistic-fuzz")

# 3) Wide regime: boundary says weights are arbitrary finite f32.
N = 10_000_000
y = to_bf16_f32(rng.normal(0, 0.01, (N, 4)))
w = (rng.normal(0, 1.0, (N, 4)) * 2).astype(F32)
s = to_bf16_f32(rng.normal(0, 0.05, N))
score(y, w, s, "wide-regime")

# 4) Targeted cancellation: shared set to ~-acc at several scales.
for scale in (0.001, 0.004, 0.02, 0.1, 1.0):
    N = 2_000_000
    y = to_bf16_f32(rng.normal(0, scale / 4, (N, 4)))
    w = (rng.dirichlet(np.ones(4), N) * 2.5).astype(F32)
    p = prods(y, w)
    acc = cand_order(p)
    delta = rng.uniform(-0.05, 0.05, N).astype(F32)
    s = to_bf16_f32((-acc * (F32(1.0) + delta)).astype(F32))
    score(y, w, s, f"cancel-scale-{scale}")
print("done")

{"content":""""boundary-3 probe part 2: pin the reference association.

lsize.y=1 and lsize.y=4 both reproduce the candidate's linear chain (IEEE add
is commutative, so operand flips are bit-identical). lsize.y=2 gives
(p3+p1)+(p2+p0) (part-1 split-2: 0.0 on captured-rows8, but the grader sees
2.0 there). lsize.y=3 gives thread0 <- {p0,p3}, thread1 <- p1, thread2 <- p2:
t=(p3+p0); t=p1+(p3+p0); t=p2+(p1+(p3+p0)). Test split-3 against captured.
"""
import numpy as np
from b3_lib import (F32, to_bf16_f32, g2_ulp, prods, cand_order, ref_right,
                    ref_split2, ref_pair, full)

def ref_split3(p):
    t0 = (p[3] + p[0]).astype(F32)
    t = (p[1] + t0).astype(F32)
    return (p[2] + t).astype(F32)

def ref_split3b(p):
    # variant: loop.next assignment in a different element order guess
    t0 = (p[0] + p[3]).astype(F32)
    t = (t0 + p[1]).astype(F32)
    return (t + p[2]).astype(F32)

REFS = {"right-leaning": ref_right, "split-2": ref_split2, "pairwise": ref_pair,
        "split-3": ref_split3, "split-3b": ref_split3b}

for f, want in (("rows1", 0.0), ("rows8", 2.0), ("rows32", 1.0)):
    z = np.load(f"models/muse-inputs/{f}.npz")
    Y = np.concatenate([np.asarray(z[f"L{i:02d}_y"]).reshape(-1, 4 * 768) for i in range(20)])
    W = np.concatenate([np.asarray(z[f"L{i:02d}_weights_in"]).reshape(-1, 4) for i in range(20)])
    S = np.concatenate([np.asarray(z[f"L{i:02d}_shared"]).reshape(-1, 768) for i in range(20)])
    R = Y.shape[0]
    y = Y.reshape(R * 768, 4).astype(F32)
    w = np.repeat(W, 768, axis=0).astype(F32)
    s = S.reshape(R * 768).astype(F32)
    p = prods(y, w)
    g = full(cand_order(p), s)
    line = f"{f} (grader {want}): "
    for name, fn in REFS.items():
        r = full(fn(p), s)
        over = g2_ulp(g.astype(np.float64), r.astype(np.float64))
        line += f"{name}={over.max():.1f} "
    print(line, flush=True)
print("done")

Confirming double-rounding correctness for the 53-to-24-bit float32 emulation.

{"content":""""boundary-3 probe part 3: FMA-contraction hypothesis.

Reference (separate mul + sum kernels) = pure mul-then-add chain, exactly.
Candidate (single Metal expression / loop) may be FP-contracted by the Metal
compiler into an FMA chain. Emulate FMA via float64 (exact: 53-bit intermediate
>= 2*24+2 makes double rounding harmless) and check which variant reproduces
the grader's 0.0/2.0/1.0 max-ULP fingerprint on captured inputs.
"""
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "/tmp")
import numpy as np
from b3_lib import F32, to_bf16_f32, g2_ulp, full

def fma32(a, b, c):
    return (a.astype(np.float64) * b.astype(np.float64) + c.astype(np.float64)).astype(F32)

def prods_exact(y, w):
    # standalone muls, one rounding each (reference multiply kernel)
    return tuple((y[:, j].astype(F32) * w[:, j].astype(F32)).astype(F32) for j in range(4))

def cand_mulchain(p):
    return (((p[0] + p[1]).astype(F32) + p[2]).astype(F32) + p[3]).astype(F32)

def cand_fma_A(y, w):
    # t0=a*w0; t1=fma(b,w1,t0); t2=fma(c,w2,t1); t3=fma(d,w3,t2) (= attempt-2 loop)
    y = y.astype(F32); w = w.astype(F32)
    t = (y[:, 0] * w[:, 0]).astype(F32)
    for j in (1, 2, 3):
        t = fma32(y[:, j], w[:, j], t)
    return t

def cand_fma_B(y, w):
    # first step contracted the other way: fma(a,w0,b*w1) then chain
    y = y.astype(F32); w = w.astype(F32)
    t = fma32(y[:, 0], w[:, 0], (y[:, 1] * w[:, 1]).astype(F32))
    for j in (2, 3):
        t = fma32(y[:, j], w[:, j], t)
    return t

def cand_fma_C(y, w):
    # pairwise fmas then add: fma(b,w1,a*w0) + fma(d,w3,c*w2)
    y = y.astype(F32); w = w.astype(F32)
    t01 = fma32(y[:, 1], w[:, 1], (y[:, 0] * w[:, 0]).astype(F32))
    t23 = fma32(y[:, 3], w[:, 3], (y[:, 2] * w[:, 2]).astype(F32))
    return (t01 + t23).astype(F32)

CANDS = {"mul-chain": None, "fma-A": cand_fma_A, "fma-B": cand_fma_B, "fma-C": cand_fma_C}

for f, want in (("rows1", 0.0), ("rows8", 2.0), ("rows32", 1.0)):
    z = np.load(f"models/muse-inputs/{f}.npz")
    Y = np.concatenate([np.asarray(z[f"L{i:02d}_y"]).reshape(-1, 4 * 768) for i in range(20)])
    W = np.concatenate([np.asarray(z[f"L{i:02d}_weights_in"]).reshape(-1, 4) for i in range(20)])
    S = np.concatenate([np.asarray(z[f"L{i:02d}_shared"]).reshape(-1, 768) for i in range(20)])
    R = Y.shape[0]
    y = Y.reshape(R * 768, 4).astype(F32)
    w = np.repeat(W, 768, axis=0).astype(F32)
    s = S.reshape(R * 768).astype(F32)
    p = prods_exact(y, w)
    r = full(cand_mulchain(p), s)  # reference: separate kernels, exact
    line = f"{f} (grader {want}): "
    for name, fn in CANDS.items():
        g = full(cand_mulchain(p) if fn is None else fn(y, w), s)
        over = g2_ulp(g.astype(np.float64), r.astype(np.float64))
        line += f"{name}={over.max():.1f}(bad={int((over > 2).sum())}) "
    print(line, flush=True)
print("done")
","path":"/tmp/b3_probe3.py"}

exact rational oracle; (b) asymmetric-pairwise fma on captured; (c) random
tree x fma-placement envelope: can ANY evaluation reach 2.0 on captured
rows8 / exceed 2 anywhere on resampled-realistic data?

import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "/tmp")
import struct
import itertools
import random
from fractions import Fraction
import numpy as np
from b3_lib import F32, to_bf16_f32, g2_ulp, full
from b3_probe3 import fma32, prods_exact, cand_mulchain

# (a) RNE oracle check
def bf16_oracle(f):
    if not np.isfinite(f):
        raise ValueError("non-finite")
    fr = Fraction(float(np.float32(f)))  # exact value of the f32 input
    sign = -1 if fr < 0 else 1
    fr = abs(fr)
    if fr == 0:
        return struct.unpack('<f', struct.pack('<I', 0x80000000 if sign < 0 else 0))[0]
    e = fr.numerator.bit_length() - fr.denominator.bit_length()  # ~log2
    # binary exponent: 2^e <= fr < 2^(e+1)
    while Fraction(2) ** e > fr:
        e -= 1
    while Fraction(2) ** (e + 1) <= fr:
        e += 1
    # bf16: 8-bit significand (1 implicit + 7); unit = 2^(e-7)
    unit = Fraction(2) ** (e - 7)
    q, r = divmod(fr, unit)  # q in [128, 255]
    q = int(q)
    half = unit / 2
    if r > half or (r == half and q % 2 == 1):
        q += 1
        if q == 256:
            q, e = 128, e + 1
    return float(sign * Fraction(q) * Fraction(2) ** (e - 7))

rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
test = np.concatenate([rng.normal(0, 0.02, 20000).astype(F32),

                                 np.float32(0.0078125)], dtype=F32)])
got = to_bf16_f32(test)
bad = 0
for i in range(len(test)):
    want = np.float32(bf16_oracle(test[i]))
    if got[i] != want and not (np.isnan(got[i]) and np.isnan(want)):
        bad += 1
        if bad < 5:
            print(f"  RNE MISMATCH {test[i]!r}: got {got[i]!r} want {want!r}", flush=True)

def add(a, b):
    return (a.astype(F32) + b.astype(F32)).astype(F32)

CAP = {}
for f in ("rows1", "rows8", "rows32"):
    z = np.load(f"models/muse-inputs/{f}.npz")
    Y = np.concatenate([np.asarray(z[f"L{i:02d}_y"]).reshape(-1, 4 * 768) for i in range(20)])
    W = np.concatenate([np.asarray(z[f"L{i:02d}_weights_in"]).reshape(-1, 4) for i in range(20)])

    fp = []
    for f in ("rows1", "rows8", "rows32"):
        y, w, s, p, r = CAP[f]
        g = full(fn(y, w), s)
        over = g2_ulp(g.astype(np.float64), r.astype(np.float64))
        fp.append(round(float(over.max()), 1))
    print(f"(b) {name}: fingerprint {fp} (grader [0.0, 2.0, 1.0])", flush=True)

# (c) random envelope: random tree shape + leaf order + fma coin flips
SHAPES = [
    lambda E, o: ('add', ('add', ('add', ('m', o[0]), ('m', o[1])), ('m', o[2])), ('m', o[3])),
    lambda E, o: ('add', ('add', ('m', o[0]), ('add', ('m', o[1]), ('m', o[2]))), ('m', o[3])),
    lambda E, o: ('add', ('m', o[0]), ('add', ('add', ('m', o[1]), ('m', o[2])), ('m', o[3]))),
    lambda E, o: ('add', ('m', o[0]), ('add', ('m', o[1]), ('add', ('m', o[2]), ('m', o[3])))),
    lambda E, o: ('add', ('add', ('m', o[0]), ('m', o[1])), ('add', ('m', o[2]), ('m', o[3]))),
]

def eval_tree(t, y, w, p, coins, ci):
    kind = t[0]

    _, L, R = t

    if coins and ((L[0] == 'm') != (R[0] == 'm')) and random.random() < 0.5:

            rv, ci = eval_tree(R, y, w, p, coins, ci)
            return fma32(y[:, j], w[:, j], rv), ci
        else:

            lv, ci = eval_tree(L, y, w, p, coins, ci)
            return fma32(y[:, j], w[:, j], lv), ci
    lv, ci = eval_tree(L, y, w, p, coins, ci)
    rv, ci = eval_tree(R, y, w, p, coins, ci)

1|# Attempt 3: two-kernel grouped experts split (builder-1-c, direction c)
2|
3|First in direction (c): kernel 1 fuses gate+up+silu-mul with grouped
4|same-expert reads; kernel 2 runs the down product with grouped reads. One
5|threadgroup per expert finds its pairs by scanning `inds`, streams each
6|weight tile once per chunk from DRAM, reuses it across the chunk. A `hidden`
7|[rows,4,384] bf16 buffer passes between the kernels in DRAM.
8|
9|## What it removes, and how
10|
11|- `ineff-quantized-kernels-1`: per-pair qvm grids re-read each expert's
12|  weights once per pair (908 MB/step at 32 rows for 443 MB distinct). Here
13|  each appearing expert's weights stream ~once per call (34 MB/layer at 32
14|  rows vs 71 MB per-pair); tile loads are coalesced.
15|- `ineff-switch-layers-2`: gate/up/activation fused (one hidden round-trip);
16|  no sort/unsort glue (`ineff-switch-layers-1`), valid at every 1-32 rows.
17|- `ineff-runs-1`: the same grouping removes the excess re-reads.
18|
19|Final structure (v7): 192/384 threads per group, 2 outputs per thread (an
20|even pair shares one weight word + one scale/bias), chunks of 2 pairs with
21|scalar accumulators, branchless inner loop (short chunks pad with pair 0's x,
22|phantom stores skipped), K unrolled x2 with even/odd accumulators.
23|
24|Threadgroup memory by hand (grader does not check 32 KB): k1 = 12 KB weight
25|tiles + 3 KB scales/biases + 128 B x tile + ~1 KB pair lists ≈ 16.1 KB; k2
26|likewise ≈ 16.1 KB. Threadgroups 192/384. All indexing valid for rows 1-32
27|(P = rows*4 ≤ 128; guarded plist reads); barriers uniform; each (pair,
28|output) written once, no atomics.
29|
30|## Predicted us per layer at 1 / 8 / 32 rows
31|
32|Weight bytes per expert (all three matrices): 552,960 B. Distinct experts
33|per layer: ~4 / ~20 / ~53 → traffic/layer ≈ 2.23 / 11.2 / 29.9 MB. At the
34|normal streaming rate 150 GB/s (ineff-quantized-kernels-1): 14.9 / 74.7 /
35|199 us + 2 launches (~10 us): **25 / 85 / 210 us per layer**.
36|
37|## Version history (same folder)

39|- v1: chunk-8 with accumulator arrays, naive silu (round once). G1 pass, G2
40|  fail (~7% bad, max 11/32/68 ULP).
41|- v2: per-op bf16 silu rounds (S2). Barely moved (~6% bad) → silu rounding
42|  placement was not (only) the issue.
43|- CPU forensics (/tmp/probe_swiglu.py, /tmp/probe_ls.py: float64 replay from
44|  captured inputs + safetensors weights, zero GPU): reproduced the grader's
45|  S1/S2 bad counts EXACTLY (4594=4594 etc.), proving dequant/products correct
46|  and isolating the gap to swiglu internals. `strings` on libmlx.dylib gave
47|  MLX's Metal Sigmoid: `y = 1/(1+precise::exp(abs(x))); return (x<0)?y:1-y`
48|  in bfloat with per-op rounds. S17 (stable form + full bf16 rounds) matched

18|- **`README.md`.** The phase's document. Only the lead writes it, refreshing it and raising its version at every checkpoint. It opens with its version line and the tracker table below.
19|- **Entries.** One file per territory, inefficiency or hypothesis. The owner keeps it current, and other agents append notes.
20|- **`log.md`.** One line per event, from every agent, appended only.
21|
22|## Versions
23|
24|Every shared document carries a version number, so a reader knows which version they're looking at, and git holds every version.
25|
26|**Phase versions.** Each README opens with its version line:
27|
28|```markdown
29|**Version:** v5 · 2026-11-04T09:40Z · skill version 3
30|```
31|
32|- **Who raises it:** the lead, at every checkpoint, and each version is exactly one commit.
33|- **The commit:** its subject names the version, `Muse Spark: exploration v5: <what changed>`. `git log --grep 'exploration v5:'` finds it, and `git diff` between two such commits shows what changed.
34|- **The changelog:** the README ends with `## Versions`, one line per version, newest first, naming the entries that changed and their new versions:
35|
36|```markdown
37|- v5 · 2026-11-04T09:40Z · split quantized-kernels in two · changed: territory-quantized-kernels v4, ineff-quantized-kernels-2 v2
38|```
39|
40|**Entry versions.** Each entry's status block has a `Version` line, starting at 1:
41|- **Territory and inefficiency entries:** the owner raises it with every change to its own text. The verifier raises it when it writes the verdict.
42|- **Hypothesis entries:** the lead raises it at each checkpoint where the entry changed, builders' and the boundary agent's sections included.
43|- **Notes:** a note under `## From other agents` leaves the version alone. The owner raises it when folding the note in.
44|
45|## The README trackers
46|
47|Exploration, `exploration/README.md`:
48|
49|| Territory | Agent | Status | Inefficiencies | Updated |
50||---|---|---|---|---|
51|| `quantized-kernels` | `explorer-quantized-kernels` | exploring | `ineff-quantized-kernels-1` (confirmed), `-2` (open) | 2026-11-04 09:40Z |
52|
53|Implementation, `implementation/README.md`:
54|
55|| Hypothesis | Slot | Builders | Attempts: G1, G2, µs per layer at 1 / 8 / 32 rows (compiled) | Status |
56||---|---|---|---|---|
57|| `hyp-1-fused-gather` | `experts` | `builder-1-a`, `builder-1-b` | 3: pass, pass, 41 / 55 / 180 (48 / 70 / 260) | hardening |
58|
59|## Entries
60|
61|Each entry opens with a status block that its owner keeps current:
62|
63|```markdown
64|- **Owner:** explorer-quantized-kernels
65|- **Status:** exploring
66|- **Version:** 3
67|- **Updated:** 2026-11-04T09:40Z
68|- **Next:** read the 32-row dispatch of affine_gather_qmm
69|```
70|
71|Entries are named so that two agents never pick the same name:
72|- `exploration/territory-<territory>.md`
73|- `exploration/ineff-<territory>-<n>.md`, numbered by the explorer of that territory
74|- `implementation/hyp-<n>-<slug>.md`, numbered by the lead
75|
76|**Another agent's entry:** append under its `## From other agents` heading, starting with your name and the time. The owner's text stays as written, so two agents never overwrite each other. The owner reads these notes and folds in what holds.
77|
78|### Territory entry
79|
80|1. Status block (statuses: `exploring`, `done`).
81|2. **What it does** in the decode step, in a few lines.
82|3. **The checklist** below, filled in for each piece of code or table in the territory.
83|4. **Relations:** which territories feed it and which it feeds, with the data passed.
84|5. **Inefficiencies:** links to the entries this territory raised.
85|6. **Files read**, and what each one gave.
86|
87|### Inefficiency entry
88|
89|1. Status block. The statuses are `open`, `confirmed`, `refuted` and `superseded by <entry>`; only the verifier sets `confirmed` or `refuted`.
90|2. **Slot:** `routing`, `combine`, `experts`, or `outside the slots`.
91|3. **What happens:** what the code does, and where (file and lines).
92|4. **Cost** at 1, 8 and 32 rows: kernels × the fixed cost per kernel, bytes ÷ peak bandwidth, and the measured time with the table it comes from.
93|5. **Kind:** overhead-bound, bandwidth-bound or compute-bound, in the terms of `claude/GLOSSARY.md`.
94|6. **Spans:** the territories involved.
95|7. **Predicted saving** if removed, in µs per decode step at 1, 8 and 32 rows, with the arithmetic.
96|8. **Verdict**, written by the verifier: each claim checked, and the result.
97|
98|### Hypothesis entry
99|
100|1. Status block. The lead owns it; the statuses are `boundary`, `building`, `hardening`, `ready` and `dropped`.
101|2. **Inefficiency** it removes, and the slot.
102|3. **Boundary**, written by the boundary agent: what the solution must keep identical (see `boundary.md`).
103|4. **One section per builder:** its direction, its attempts (folder, predicted and measured µs per layer at 1, 8 and 32 rows, G1, G2), and what each attempt taught.
104|5. **Boundary checks** of the attempts that passed G2.
105|6. **Decision:** the best attempt and why. When the status is `ready`, it states what G3 should show.
106|
107|## The checklist
108|
109|Fill it in for each piece of code you inspect, so that no piece is judged without its neighbours:
110|
111|- **Callers:** who calls it, and with what shapes at 1, 8 and 32 rows.
112|- **Callees:** what it calls, down to the Metal kernel it launches.
113|- **Data:** each input and output with shape, dtype and layout. Where it is produced, and where it is consumed next.
114|- **Neighbours:** what runs just before and after it in the decode step, and what a replacement must keep identical.
115|- **Cost:** the kernels it launches, the bytes it reads and writes (weight bytes counted per read), and its measured time with the table the time comes from.
116|- **Invariants:** what correctness depends on: the G2 tolerances, the tie rule for the 4th and 5th expert, the bfloat16 rounding points.
117|
118|## The log
119|
120|Append one line per event with the shell, so lines from several agents never mix:
121|
122|```bash
123|printf '%s | %s | %s\n' "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" "explorer-quantized-kernels" "posted ineff-quantized-kernels-2: each weight byte read 4 times at 32 rows" >> muse-spark/exploration/log.md
124|```
125|
126|Log when you start, claim something, post or confirm an entry, change direction (what from, what to, and which entry made you), grade an attempt (with its verdict), and finish.
127|
128|## Adapting to the others' work
129|
130|Before every new piece of work, and after every post:
131|1. Read the phase README's tracker and the newest 30 lines of the phase log (`tail -n 30`).
132|2. Then change direction when:
133|   - **someone else covers it:** another entry already covers the same code or cause, so append to that entry instead of starting a second one;
134|   - **its premise fell:** the claim your work rests on was refuted;
135|   - **something pays more:** an open item in your territory or task predicts a larger saving than what you're on, and nobody owns it.
136|3. When you change direction, log it with the reason, and write it in your own entry's status block.
137|
138|Two claims on the same item go to the lead, who settles them.
139|
140|## Rules for every agent
141|
142|- **Writes go only to `muse-spark/`, in the files your role names.** Everything else in the worktree, and everything outside it, is read-only.
143|- **Only the lead commits.** Helpers never run `git add` or `git commit`.
144|- **The grader is the only GPU job.** Run it only as a builder, through the brief's command; it waits its turn when another run has the GPU. Load no model and start no other GPU work: the machine has 16 GB and slows down sharply when memory runs short.
145|- **Every number has a source:** a file and line, a table (path and row), a grader verdict (attempt folder), or arithmetic shown in full.
146|- **Credentials stay unread:** `.env` files, `~/.config/muse/` and any key store.
147|- **The API-stage kernels** in the history before the tag `agent-era` are from an earlier, removed stage (PROVENANCE.md) and stay unread.

Read text file `muse-spark/implementation/hyp-1-fused-experts.md`.
1|# Hypothesis 1: fused grouped experts kernel
2|
3|- **Owner:** lead
4|- **Status:** hardening
5|- **Version:** 6
6|- **Updated:** 2026-11-03T22:45:00Z
7|- **Next:** best is attempt-2 (only beats_compiled=true, bit-exact, boundary pass); builder-1-d hardening it with one change (1-row occupancy); boundary-1 checking attempt-1
8|
9|## Inefficiency
10|
11|Slot `experts`. One combined fix for five confirmed entries (savings do not add; joint ceiling 443 MB at streaming rate ≈ 11.5 ms at 32 rows, per the verifier):
12|
13|- `ineff-quantized-kernels-1` (rank 1, mean 19.9% of step): per-pair qvm grids at ~1/3 peak; ideal 0.5 / 2.5 / 8.6 ms at 1/8/32 rows.
14|- `ineff-findings-2` (rank 3, mean 10.4%): measured 25% grouped-kernel win; 0.40 / 1.30 / 3.67 ms.
15|- `ineff-switch-layers-2` (rank 4, mean 4.3%): unfused products+activation; ~0.4 ms at all row counts.
16|- `ineff-runs-1` (rank 6, mean 4.2%): 465 MB excess re-reads; floor 0.0 / 0.6 / 2.3 ms.
17|- `ineff-switch-layers-1` (rank 7, mean 0.8%): sort glue 0.7 ms at 32 rows, removable only inside this fix.
18|
19|Design: one Metal kernel that batches same-expert pairs with coalesced reads, runs gate/up/down plus the activation with intermediates on-chip, and needs no sort/unsort. Must keep the G2 boundary (2 bf16 ULP, fp32 accumulation, bf16 rounding points).
20|
21|## Boundary
22|
23|(written by boundary-1; every line carries its source)
24|
25|### Inputs and outputs
26|
27|Sources: the brief's `experts` slot section (`claude/muse-agent-brief.md:70-92`) and `bench/grader/slots.py:19-40,271`. Constants `D,E,K,H = 768,60,4,384` (slots.py:19; brief:26). All arrays row-contiguous (brief:24). `rows` is read from the first slot input's `shape[0]` (slots.py:271); any 1–32 in decode (brief:24).
28|
29|| Name | Shape at 1 / 8 / 32 rows | Dtype | Layout / notes |
30||---|---|---|---|
31|| `x` | [1,768] / [8,768] / [32,768] | bfloat16 | brief:74 |
32|| `inds` | [1,4] / [8,4] / [32,4] | uint32 | brief:75; cast to u32 on load, slots.py:219-220 |
33|| `gate_w`, `up_w` | [60,768,48], rows-independent | uint32 | [expert,in,out] transposed layout (brief:76; mobilemoe.py:42,202-214); 8 4-bit values per word along out; output column `o` sits in word `o/8` at bits `4*(o%8)` (brief:82) |
34|| `gate_scales`, `gate_biases`, `up_scales`, `up_biases` | [60,768,12] each, rows-independent | bfloat16 | one scale and bias per 32 outputs (brief:77); `w = scale*q + bias`, affine, group_size 32, bits 4 (brief:82; slots.py:67-77) |
35|| `down_w` | [60,384,96], rows-independent | uint32 | same packing as gate/up (brief:78) |
36|| `down_scales`, `down_biases` | [60,384,24] each, rows-independent | bfloat16 | one scale and bias per 32 outputs (brief:79) |
37|| `y` (output) | [1,4,768] / [8,4,768] / [32,4,768] | bfloat16 | brief:80; `y[r,j]` is expert `inds[r,j]`'s output, positional (see neighbour B) |
38|
39|Weight bytes per layer (arithmetic shown): gate/up/down `_w` are each 60·768·48 = 60·384·96 = 2,211,840 words = 8,847,360 B; gate/up/down scales and biases are each 60·768·12 = 60·384·24 = 552,960 values = 1,105,920 B. Total ≈ 3·(8,847,360 + 2·1,105,920) ≈ 33.2 MB per layer, shared by all rows.
40|The spec's `slot_outputs` must provide `y` (slots.py:266-268). Grid counts threads, not threadgroups (slots.py:283).
41|
42|### Before and after
43|
44|Source: `MoE.__call__` (`third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/mobilemoe.py:217-232`) and the split MoE the grader installs (`bench/grader/slots.py:97-119`, bit-identical to the port per `check_identity`, slots.py:122-134). Order per layer: post_attention_layernorm → `x`; router → `inds`, `weights`; experts(`x`, `inds`) → `y`; shared_expert(`x`) → `shared` (independent of this slot, runs alongside); combine(`y`, `weights`, `shared`) → `out` → residual / next layer (mobilemoe.py:230-232,257-258; slots.py:105-118). The grader flattens model `[B,L,D]` to `[rows,D]` and restores shapes afterwards (brief:24; slots.py:106-117).
45|
46|Neighbour A — what produces the slot's inputs (layernorm + routing), per tracking.md checklist:
47|- **Callers:** `MoE.__call__` in all 20 layers of every decode step (mobilemoe.py:217-230; brief:24).
48|- **Callees:** router Linear in float32, sigmoid, `argpartition(-biased, kth=3)`, `take_along_axis`, normalize `+1e-20` then `×2.5` (slots.py:44-48; mobilemoe.py:219-228).
49|- **Data:** `x` is bf16 RMSNorm output, flattened [rows,768]; `inds` is u32 [rows,4], 4 distinct experts per row in arbitrary order, values in [0,60) (slots.py:44-48; routing G2 rejects inds ≥ 60, check_candidate.py:65).
50|- **Neighbours:** this slot must accept `inds` in ANY order, including either side of a routing near-tie: within-row order is free (brief:47) and routing G2 matches expert sets, skipping rows whose 4th/5th biased scores are within 1e-6 (check_candidate.py:71-80).
51|- **Cost:** routing's own ~12 kernels/layer (brief:47) — not this slot's cost.
52|- **Invariants:** `inds` valid [0,60); `x` finite bf16; row count any 1–32 (brief:24), not just 1/8/32.
53|
54|Neighbour B — what consumes `y` (combine + residual), per tracking.md checklist:
55|- **Callers:** combine is called as `combine(y.reshape(-1,K,D), weights, shared.reshape(-1,D))` (slots.py:116).
56|- **Callees:** `(y * weights[...,None]).sum(axis=-2).astype(bf16) + shared` (slots.py:51-52; mobilemoe.py:231-232).
57|- **Data:** `y` [rows,4,768] bf16 "in `inds` order" (brief:53); `weights` [rows,4] f32; `shared` [rows,768] bf16; `out` [rows,768] bf16 → reshaped to lead dims, added to the residual, fed to the next layer (slots.py:116-117).
58|- **Neighbours:** combine pairs `y[...,j,:]` with `weights[...,j]` POSITIONALLY (slots.py:52), so `y[r,j]` MUST be the output of expert `inds[r,j]` — no reordering of the K axis is visible downstream. Slot-edge traffic floor: `y` (rows·6144 B per layer) is written here and re-read by combine; ≈0.04 ms/step at 32 rows, unremovable within the interface (`territory-grader.md`, Boundary floor).
59|- **Cost:** combine's own 5 kernels/layer (brief:64) — not this slot's cost.
60|- **Invariants:** `y` must have the exact shape and bf16 dtype or G2 fails (check_candidate.py:117-118).
61|
62|### What must stay identical
63|
64|- **Reference math:** for each row `r` and `j`, with `e = inds[r,j]`: `y[r,j] = (silu(x[r] @ Wgate[e]) * (x[r] @ Wup[e])) @ Wdown[e]` (brief:84-88); port code `ref_experts` (slots.py:55-82) with `swiglu(gate,x) = silu(gate)*x` (activations.py:9-11), `gather_qmm(..., transpose=False, group_size=32, bits=4, mode="affine")` (slots.py:67-77).
65|- **Rounding points:** each gate/up/down product accumulates in float32 and rounds its output to bfloat16; `silu(gate)*up` is computed on those bfloat16 values and rounded to bfloat16 before the down product (brief:90). Keep fp32 accumulation (nothing narrower) and all four bf16 rounding points (carry no wider precision across them) — this hypothesis's stated G2 boundary.
66|- **Tie rule:** there is NONE inside this slot — instead the slot inherits routing's freedom: it must handle any 4 valid expert ids per row in any order, never assuming sorted `inds` or the reference `argpartition` order (brief:47; check_candidate.py:71-80).
67|- **Allowed reorderings:** any summation order inside fp32 accumulation; any grouping of (row, expert) pairs and any thread/block decomposition; sort or no sort at ANY row count including ≥16 (the reference sorts iff `inds.size >= 64`, slots.py:62, switch_layers.py:181, but G2 compares outputs only, so the choice is free — `territory-grader.md` note on ineff-runs-3); any dequantization order. **Forbidden:** moving any `y` element off its `[r,j,d]` position, changing shapes/dtypes, narrowing accumulation below fp32, skipping a bf16 rounding, or fusing across the slot edges (`x`/`inds` in, `y` out stay in DRAM between slots).
68|
69|### What the grader checks, and what it can't see
70|
71|Checks (`bench/grader/check_candidate.py`):
72|- **G1:** compiles and runs on real inputs at 1, 8 and 32 rows (`g1=True` after the loops, 206; any exception → error + g1 false, 227-228, Metal errors trimmed by `short_error`, 153-163). Note: shape/dtype mismatches are per-layer stats, not exceptions — they fail G2 with g1 true (188-191).
73|- **G2 experts** (`check_experts`, 112-130): exact shape [rows,4,768] and bf16 dtype (117-118); EVERY element within 2 bf16 ULP of the reference, with the ULP floored at |r| = 0.001 so reorderings near zero don't fail (`ulp_bf16`, 44-47; 119-123). All 20 layers' captured inputs at each of 1/8/32 rows must pass (179-205). Inputs are seeded (`mx.random.seed(rows)`, slots.py:158) — deterministic every run.
74|- **Piece timing** runs only if G2 passes (209-226): median of 30 repeats of all-20-layer evals, per layer; `beats_compiled` needs candidate < compiled reference at ALL three row counts. "It is a guide; G3 decides" (brief:193).
75|What it can't see (checked by hand later — boundary.md *check an attempt*):
76|- Row counts other than 1, 8 and 32: any 1–32 occur in decode (brief:24); grids and indexing must be valid for all of them.
77|- Inputs beyond the captured set: one seeded run of 128-token random prompts, decode step 8 (slots.py:158-168). Real prompts, steps and activation distributions differ — no assumption fitted to the captured values survives.
78|- Reads of threadgroup memory never written, results that depend on thread timing, out-of-bounds reads that luckily pass, threadgroup memory over 32 KB (`build` enforces only the thread COUNT, slots.py:274-276, not the 32 KB).
79|- End-to-end and G3, run after merge (`time_candidates.py`): the same greedy tokens over 24 generated tokens at 1 and 32 requests in plain MLX and vLLM (brief:185), and a lower decode-step period than both the original and the compiled reference with the gap exceeding the repeat spread (brief:186).
80|
81|### The GPU limits
82|
83|- At most 1,024 threads per threadgroup (brief:98; count enforced in slots.py:275) and 32 KB of threadgroup memory (brief:98; NOT enforced by `build` — verify by hand from the Metal source).
84|- Grid counts threads (slots.py:283); sizes are ints or products of ints and rows/D/E/K/H only (slots.py:230-240); dtypes float32/bfloat16/float16/uint32/int32 (slots.py:22-28).
85|- Only `mx.fast.metal_kernel`, MLX 0.32.4; the grader runs no Python of the candidate's — the spec is data, only the Metal compiles (brief:96-97). A grader run should take under 3 minutes (brief:98).
86|- Hardware: Apple M1 Pro GPU, 16 cores, SIMD width 32, bfloat16 as `bfloat` in Metal (brief:99).
87|
88|## Builders
89|
90|### builder-1-b — direction (b): fusion first, keeping per-pair reads
91|
92|One threadgroup per (row, expert-slot) pair; gate/up share one K-loop over an
93|on-chip x row; gate/up/hidden in threadgroup memory (3840 B); weights read
94|once per pair, no batching, no sort. Numerics replicate the reference
95|bitwise: qvm strided-lane accumulation + `simd_sum` per 32-output block, and
96|silu computed ENTIRELY in bf16 (round after exp/add/recip/sub/mul/mul —
97|found by CPU search over all 64 rounding placements, only full-bf16 matches).
98|
99|- attempt-2 (`muse-spark/kernels/experts/attempt-2`, v3): predicted 30 / 185 /
100|  470 µs per layer at 1/8/32 rows; measured 107.3 / 188.4 / 647.6 (original
101|  99.8 / 218.7 / 768.6; compiled 135.0 / 216.9 / 761.7). G1 pass; G2 pass
102|  with max_ulp 0.0 at all rows (bit-exact); beats_compiled true at all rows.
103|- Taught: (1) down outputs near cancellation amplify hidden 1-ULP flips, so
104|  gate/up/hidden must match bitwise — any summation order will NOT do;
105|  (2) MLX's compiled swiglu rounds every op to bf16 (all other builders must
106|  replicate this); (3) rows-1 is occupancy-bound (512 threads, 20 GB/s
107|  effective), not streaming — fusion alone regresses 7.5% vs eager there;
108|  (4) no cross-pair cache reuse at 32 rows (full 70.8 MB/layer @ ~109 GB/s).
109|
110|### builder-1-c — direction (c): TWO-kernel split with grouped same-expert reads
111|
112|Kernel 1 fuses gate+up+silu-mul, kernel 2 the down product; one threadgroup
113|per expert (60 groups) finds its pairs by scanning `inds` and streams each
114|weight tile once per 2-pair chunk (~34 MB/layer at 32 rows vs 71 MB
115|per-pair). Final form (v7): 192/384 threads, 2 outputs per thread (an even
116|pair shares one weight word + one scale/bias), branchless padded chunks,
117|K unrolled x2 with even/odd accumulators. Tmem ~16.1 KB per kernel by hand.
118|Numerics: MLX's stable bfloat Sigmoid bit-exact
119|(`y=1/(1+precise::exp(abs(x)))`, `(x<0)?y:1-y`, per-op bf16 rounds — read
120|from libmlx.dylib, verified on CPU against all 2.5M captured outputs).
121|
122|- attempt-3 (`muse-spark/kernels/experts/attempt-3`, v7): predicted 25 / 85 /
123|  210 µs per layer at 1/8/32 rows; measured 68.1 / 238.4 / 654.1 (original
124|  70.0 / 214.7 / 769.8; compiled 64.9 / 213.1 / 764.0). G1 pass; G2 pass
125|  with max_ulp 1.0 at all rows; beats_compiled false (wins 32 rows ~15%,
126|  misses 1 row by 5% / 8 rows by 12%).
127|- Taught: (1) dynamic-index accumulator arrays spill to stack (~10x slow);
128|  unroll with scalars; (2) per-iteration guards + 8x loop bloat eat all
129|  tile-sharing gains — chunk-2 padded branchless wins because pairs/expert
130|  is always ~1-2.4; (3) tiled load→barrier→compute halves DRAM duty cycle
131|  (~55 GB/s achieved vs 150 ideal); (4) at 8 rows grouping's DRAM edge
132|  barely outweighs padding waste — hardening should hybridize with
133|  attempt-2's per-pair win (188 µs at 8 rows).
134|
135|### builder-1-a — direction (a): full fused grouped kernel (ONE kernel)
136|
137|One threadgroup per expert (60 groups) scans `inds` for its pairs and runs
138|gate/up/down + silu-mul fused with intermediates on-chip, no sort/unsort.
139|v1-v9 replicated the reference bit-exactly (qvm strided lanes + `simd_sum`,
140|per-op bf16 silu derived from MLX source); v10+ reused attempt-3's
141|G2-proven even/odd-split + tmem-tile forms. Final (v14): 192 threads,
142|chunks of 2 pairs, gate/up = attempt-3 k1 shape, down = k2 per-thread
143|shape over 2 output blocks. Tmem ~17.1 KB by hand.
144|
145|- attempt-1 (`muse-spark/kernels/experts/attempt-1`, v14 final of v1-v15):
146|  predicted 35 / 100 / 220 µs per layer at 1/8/32 rows; measured 79.3 /
147|  260.3 / 743.7 (original 64.1 / 214.4 / 767.1; compiled 62.0 / 214.1 /
148|  761.0). G1 pass; G2 pass with max_ulp 1.0, bad 0; beats_compiled false
149|  (beats compiled only at 32 rows). Full version log + analysis in
150|  `attempt-1/notes.md`.
151|- Taught: (1) bit-exact qvm replication passes G2 at max_ulp 0.0 but runs
152|  ~1/2.3 reference throughput — the strided-lane structure is unfixable
153|  (threads/unroll/scalars/coalescing all verified neutral by grade);
154|  (2) G2 does NOT need bitwise products: even/odd split + plain dequant +
155|  bfloat silu passes (max 1.0), and all three builders' v1s failed
156|  identically (max 11/32/68 ULP) on the five bf16 rounding points of the
157|  compiled swiglu alone; (3) wider sharing backfires: C=4 (+21-50%) and
158|  384 threads cost more in tmem reads/pressure than they share —
159|  2-pair chunks at 192 threads are the sweet spot; (4) vs attempt-2
160|  (107.3/188.4/647.6): fusion-without-grouping wins at 8/32 rows because
161|  grouping's byte savings don't convert in the piece harness (cache
162|  absorbs re-reads) while scan/chunk/barrier/phantom overhead is real —
163|  hardening should start from attempt-2 and add grouping only on G3
164|  cache-pressure evidence.
165|
166|## Boundary checks
167|
168|- **attempt-2 — pass** (boundary-1): one fused per-pair kernel, G2 bit-exact. Checked

7|## The task
8|
9|Meta's MobileMoE-S, int4, is served on an Apple M1 Pro (16-core GPU, 200 GB/s, 16 GB) by vLLM through vllm-metal, which runs the model with MLX. The findings below measure where each decode step's time goes. A step is about 870–1,090 small GPU kernels and is far from both the bandwidth and compute limits. The findings name the pieces that cost the most.
10|
11|1. **Choose.** Read the findings and choose one or two of the slots below to replace with your own fused Metal kernels. Write `muse-spark/strategy.md`: why, your design, and what each saves per step at 1 and 32 requests (your estimate). End it with the JSON block described under *Your files*. Commit it.
12|2. **Write and check.** For each chosen slot, write the kernels as files, run the grader on them, read its verdict, and improve. Up to **5 attempts per slot**; an attempt is a folder you graded and committed.
13|3. **Finish.** Write `muse-spark/summary.md`: your final attempt per slot and what you learned. Commit it.
14|
15|**Read these first** (all in your worktree):
16|- `claude/findings/bottleneck-explained.md` and `claude/findings/step-breakdown.md`: the measured findings;
17|- `results/runs/2026-11-01-breakdown/tables.md` and `results/runs/2026-11-02-gpu-counters/tables.md`: the raw tables;
18|- `third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/mobilemoe.py` and `switch_layers.py`: the model code;
19|- MLX's custom-kernel documentation: `.venv/bin/python -c "import mlx.core as mx; help(mx.fast.metal_kernel)"`;
20|- `bench/grader/check_candidate.py` and `bench/grader/slots.py`: how you are graded.
21|
22|## The slots
23|
24|Each slot is a piece of the mixture-of-experts block, `MoE.__call__` in `mobilemoe.py`, which runs in all 20 layers of every step. `rows` is the number of tokens in the step: 1 to 32 in decode. The grader flattens the inputs to the shapes below and restores the model's shapes afterwards. All arrays are row-contiguous.
25|
26|The model's constants: hidden size `D = 768`, experts `E = 60`, experts per token `K = 4`, expert hidden size `H = 384`, `routed_scaling_factor = 2.5`, `norm_topk_prob = true`.
27|
28|### `routing`: router, top-4 selection and weights
29|
30|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
31||---|---|---|---|
32|| input | `x` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
33|| input | `w_router` | [60, 768] | float32 |
34|| input | `bias` | [60] | float32 (the model's bfloat16 `expert_bias`, converted exactly) |
35|| output | `inds` | [rows, 4] | uint32 |
36|| output | `weights` | [rows, 4] | float32 |
37|
38|Reference:
39|
40|```python
41|scores = mx.sigmoid(x.astype(mx.float32) @ w_router.T)          # [rows, 60]
42|inds = mx.argpartition(-(scores + bias), kth=3, axis=-1)[:, :4]  # the 4 largest biased scores
43|w = mx.take_along_axis(scores, inds, axis=-1)                    # unbiased scores of those 4
44|weights = w / (w.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True) + 1e-20) * 2.5
45|```
46|
47|The order of the 4 experts within a row is free, as long as `weights[r, j]` belongs to `inds[r, j]`. Today this slot is about 12 kernels per layer, 240 per step. It costs 1.02 ms of a 4.75 ms step at 1 request and 1.68 ms at 32 requests.
48|
49|### `combine`: weighting the routed experts' outputs and adding the shared expert
50|
51|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
52||---|---|---|---|
53|| input | `y` | [rows, 4, 768] | bfloat16 (the 4 experts' outputs, in `inds` order) |
54|| input | `weights` | [rows, 4] | float32 |
55|| input | `shared` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 (the shared expert's output) |
56|| output | `out` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
57|
58|Reference:
59|
60|```python
61|out = (y * weights[..., None]).sum(axis=-2).astype(mx.bfloat16) + shared
62|```
63|
64|Today this slot is 5 kernels per layer, 100 per step. It costs 0.61 ms at 1 request and 0.33 ms at 32 requests.
65|
66|### `routing+combine`
67|
68|Both slots above, each with its own kernels, in one candidate.
69|
70|### `experts`: the routed experts' three quantized products
71|
72|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
73||---|---|---|---|
74|| input | `x` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
75|| input | `inds` | [rows, 4] | uint32 |
76|| input | `gate_w`, `up_w` | [60, 768, 48] | uint32 (4-bit weights in [expert, in, out] layout, 8 per word along out) |
77|| input | `gate_scales`, `gate_biases`, `up_scales`, `up_biases` | [60, 768, 12] | bfloat16 (one scale and bias per 32 outputs) |
78|| input | `down_w` | [60, 384, 96] | uint32 |
79|| input | `down_scales`, `down_biases` | [60, 384, 24] | bfloat16 |
80|| output | `y` | [rows, 4, 768] | bfloat16 |
81|
82|Each weight is `w = scale * q + bias`, with `q` the 4-bit value. In MLX's affine quantization, the value for output column `o` sits in word `o / 8` at bits `4 * (o % 8)`.
83|
84|Reference: for each row `r` and each `j`, with `e = inds[r, j]`:
85|
86|```python
87|y[r, j] = (silu(x[r] @ Wgate[e]) * (x[r] @ Wup[e])) @ Wdown[e]
88|```
89|
90|As in MLX's `gather_qmm(..., transpose=False)`, each product accumulates in float32 and rounds its output to bfloat16. `silu(gate) * up` is computed on those bfloat16 values, and its result is rounded to bfloat16 before the down product.
91|
92|Today this slot is 7 kernels per layer at 1 request and 13 at 32 requests (from 16 rows, MLX also sorts the pairs by expert). It costs 0.92 ms at 1 request and 14.67 ms of a 28.19 ms step at 32 requests, half the step. It reads each expert once per (token, expert) pair.
93|

183|   - **`routing`:** each row selects the same 4 experts. The only exception is a row whose 4th and 5th biased scores in the reference are within 1e-6 of each other; such rows are counted and reported. The weights, matched by expert, are within 1e-4 relative.
184|   - **`combine` and `experts`:** every element is within 2 bfloat16 units in the last place of the reference value. For values smaller than 0.001 in magnitude, the unit at 0.001 applies, so summing in a different order near zero is not a failure.

1|# attempt-4: harden attempt-2 — 256 threads per pair (builder-1-d)
2|
3|Single change on `../attempt-2` (direction b, one fused per-pair kernel):
4|256 threads per threadgroup (8 simdgroups) instead of 128 (4 simdgroups).
5|Grid goes from `rows*512` to `rows*1024` threads = still `rows*4` groups,
6|one per (row, expert-slot) pair. `block-1.metal` (qvm_block) is byte-identical
7|to attempt-2; only the wave structure in `block-0.metal` changed: gate/up 12
8|blocks in 2 waves of 8 (4 simds idle in wave 2, guarded by simd-uniform
9|`b < 12`), down 24 blocks in 3 waves of 8, x/silu strided loops step 256.
10|
11|Removes the 1-row half of attempt-2's occupancy finding (its notes.md miss
12|analysis): at 1 row, 4 pairs x 128 threads = 512 threads on a 16-core GPU
13|streams at only ~20 GB/s effective (2.21 MB in 107.3 us), regressing 7.5%
14|vs eager (99.8 us). Doubling threads per pair doubles each group's in-flight
15|memory parallelism while keeping the proven-correct numerics untouched: same
16|qvm strided-lane accumulation + `simd_sum` per 32-output block (guard is
17|uniform inside each simd, so the reduction stays uniform), same full-bf16
18|silu lowering, same fp32 accumulation and bf16 rounding points. Gate/up/down
19|weight bytes per pair are unchanged (553 KB), so 8/32 rows — already
20|streaming at ~94-109 GB/s — should be unaffected.
21|
22|Boundary kept: same as attempt-2 (boundary-1 pass): fp32 accumulation, all
23|four bf16 rounding points, positional `y[r,j]`, any `inds` order, valid for
24|all 1-32 rows (grid is `rows*4` groups, no rows-dependent indexing),
25|256 threads/group <= 1024, threadgroup memory unchanged at 3840 B (~12% of
26|32 KB).
27|
28|## Predicted us per layer at 1 / 8 / 32 rows
29|
30|- 1 row: occupancy-bound regime, threads 512 -> 1024. Effective bandwidth
31|  should roughly double from attempt-2's 20.6 GB/s (2.21 MB / 107.3 us):
32|  2.21 MB / 41 GB/s = 54 us + one launch ~7 us -> **60 us**
33|  (attempt-2 107.3; eager original 99.8; compiled 135.0). Beats eager.
34|- 8 rows: streaming regime already (17.7 MB in 188.4 us = 94 GB/s);
35|  same bytes, wider groups neutral -> **185 us**
36|  (attempt-2 188.4; original 218.7; compiled 216.9).
37|- 32 rows: same argument, full 70.8 MB at ~109 GB/s -> **650 us**
38|  (attempt-2 647.6; original 768.6; compiled 761.7).
39|
40|G2: expect bit-exact (max_ulp 0.0) — every block's computation is identical
41|to attempt-2's v3, only the wave packing changed. beats_compiled: expect
42|true at all rows.
43|
44|## Verdict
45|
46|G1 pass; G2 pass with max_ulp 0.0 at all row counts (bit-exact vs reference,
47|as predicted); beats_compiled true. Piece timing us/layer (candidate vs
48|original vs compiled, this run): rows 1: 50.0 / 64.3 / 65.3; rows 8: 157.8 /
49|218.6 / 217.4; rows 32: 515.4 / 765.7 / 760.2. Beats BOTH the eager original
50|and the compiled reference at all rows (~22/28/33% over eager, ~23/27/32%
51|over compiled). The 1-row regression is fixed: 50.0 us vs attempt-2's 107.3
52|(2.1x), now beating eager's 64.3 by 22%.
53|
54|Note: this run's 1-row baselines (64.3/65.3) are lower than attempt-2's run
55|(99.8/135.0) — the 1-row harness timing shifts between runs (attempt-1's
56|re-grade also saw 64.1/62.0), so cross-run candidate comparisons at 1 row
57|carry that caveat; within this run the candidate beats both baselines
58|cleanly. At 8/32 rows the baselines are stable across runs (218.6/217.4 vs
59|218.7/216.9; 765.7/760.2 vs 768.6/761.7), so the 8/32-row gains are real.
60|
61|## Miss analysis (prediction 60 / 185 / 650)
62|
63|Measured 50.0 / 157.8 / 515.4 — faster than predicted at all rows: -17% /
64|-15% / -21%. Only 32 rows exceeds the 20% bar, and on the fast side.
65|
66|Why: the change did more than add 1-row occupancy. Eight blocks in flight
67|per wave per group (vs four) raised per-core memory-level parallelism in
68|EVERY regime: 32-row effective bandwidth went from attempt-2's ~109 GB/s
69|(70.8 MB / 647.6 us) to ~137 GB/s (70.8 MB / 515.4 us). Attempt-2 was mildly
70|MLP-bound even where it looked streaming-bound; the extra in-flight
71|weight/scale/bias loads per group hide more latency, and halving the wave
72|count halves barrier round-trips. Same mechanism explains the 8-row (-15%)
73|and 1-row (-17%) overshoots. Lesson for `ineff-quantized-kernels-1`: per-pair
74|qvm throughput scales with in-flight blocks per group up to at least 8
75|simds, not just with group count.
